finding: Single central figure with ~35% empty grid paper on top; title sits in the top empty zone, so the eye goes title then face then hand

finding: Near-monochrome halftone photo plus cream paper with a faint grid; no colour accent at all, black night band gives contrast

finding: Orange circle sits behind a pile of monuments held in a hand; the hand overlaps the disc edge and breaks out of it at the bottom

use_when: one concept made of many objects

finding: Engraving-style (hatch) hand and buildings, cut tight, no outline, no shadow; scale deliberately wrong (hand holds a tower)

finding: Top-down desk: grid paper, stacked polaroids with white borders and tilt of ~5-8 degrees, paper clip, sticky note labels in yellow; Vox logo bottom centre

finding: Two label types: serif title on a yellow sticky strip and a typewriter-style caption on a yellow tape strip, each slightly rotated (~-2 to 3 deg)

finding: Soft vignette darkening at bottom and edges, paper texture and drop shadows under each card

finding: Brain, eye, TV, record, flag, mic scattered around a title with a hand-drawn loop line joining them; all objects greyscale engraving, title is the only colour (yellow)

finding: Title on a rough torn-brush yellow rectangle with a heavy italic serif, sub word in bold sans at a quarter of the size

finding: Objects are cut as clean silhouettes with some torn paper fragments (black shard, grey triangle) mixed in

finding: Busy template: yellow circle with logo centre, small notes, handwritten scribbles, a statue bust right, a camera top right; dense but each element is small and pushed to the edges, middle stays clear

finding: Diagonal beam from lower left to upper right with the dome, a head in a white circle on the right; crane lines and a rotated block give strong diagonals

finding: Layering has 3 depths: paper-torn strips on top, photos in the middle, a dark film-strip timeline at the bottom; headline block on the left, photos on the right

finding: Headline uses a yellow brush swab behind bold condensed black type; sub-title white box with black text; body in tiny sans; labels in typewriter

finding: Map base (cream, labels small) with red circles holding app logos, hands and phone cutout in a grey photo block; red line zig-zag crosses the frame

finding: Circle stickers are cut off at the frame edge on left and right; cropping at edges implies the scene continues

finding: Spoken line shown as a black box with white sans text plus one word on a mustard highlight; box overlaps the portrait at the chin

finding: Background text in several scripts is faint grey and half-covered, a faint ghost word is cut off by the portrait; acts as texture, not as content

finding: Figure with object replacing the head, starburst behind it (mustard) and a brown diagonal slab below; small dark disc and thin line as accents

finding: Cream paper with soft grain; photo is greyscale with a slight warm tint

finding: Two stacked TVs, symmetric, screens filled with flat blue and a hand each; background a flat mauve-grey with grain, large empty margin

finding: Hand photos are B&W duotoned and the TV is B&W photo; one saturated colour on the screens

finding: Big figure fills the left and centre; three portrait photos in tilted frames each with a typewriter nameplate sit around him; brain sketches and handwriting behind

finding: Halftone dots and handwriting texture behind, teal and orange blocks as colour fields; orange tie echoes the orange frame

finding: Small figure about 25% of the frame on a pale paper with a large red disc behind; tiny text at top and bottom and at left/right edges

finding: Figure has a red offset outline (like misregistration) on the left, a thin shadow below

finding: Flat deep teal ground, B&W photo hand, red screen, a red offset outline around the cut; black ink-blob shapes behind the phone

finding: White paper edge around the cut and a red line offset on the outer edge, shadow-free; ink blobs behind add depth

finding: Vertical stack: head, typing hands, window, laptop down a centre axis, linked by thin circuit lines and small dots

finding: Each object has a white die-cut border (about 4-6px) irregular and slightly wavy, and halftone dot photo treatment; objects in one scale band

finding: Objects roughly equal size scattered with even gaps, one large camera-hand anchors bottom left

finding: Condensed slab display type in cream on distressed red; top third, two lines, tight leading

finding: Warm grey paper, one orange accent in 3 spots (glow, bar, tag); the rest B&W

finding: Red grunge ground with black bars and dot columns; torn edges have a white fibre rim

finding: Two large faces left, oil rig and red triangle behind, right-hand text column; the faces overlap the triangle

finding: Newsprint in a warm tint with the halftone black; yellow and blue accents small

finding: Warm cream/sepia paper with fine grain and ink splatters; orange is the single accent

finding: Archive B&W desk scenes, slow stepped push-in; a yellow label on 'Weizenbaum' name and a green-glow CRT terminal; Weizenbaum portrait gets red-orange colour accent on the face
why_it_works: a single colour wash on the key face

finding: Caption is a quiet low-contrast thin serif placed at the 15% mark; key words get a yellow highlighter bar ('patterns', 'turned your') and the bar sits half a line high so letters overlap the yellow
why_it_works: highlighter bar overlapping text is a real-marker look

finding: Computer parts exploded: circuit-board sheets slide out from the monitor like cards, then the CRT sits back; flows consistent: object splits, labels, reassembles
why_it_works: exploded-view with paper cards

finding: Page-curl transition (paper page peels at the corner) between two flowchart sheets, 'Computers can't communicate with people', then newspaper clipping; the sheets are brighter than the rest
why_it_works: page curl = turn to the document

style: tan paper, grey archive, yellow bar

finding: Alternates photo scenes (1.5-3 s) with full-bleed blank cream-paper cards carrying one line of type (~1.5 s each); the paper card acts as a breath between image bursts and as the chapter mark ('1653', 'Build a wall', 'It takes weeks')
why_it_works: empty paper resets the eye so the next dense image reads as new; pace is steady, not frantic
use_when: a line is a pure statement/date and needs weight without a picture

finding: Every shot has a slow continuous camera move on a flat/graded image (32 of 36 shots flagged stepped = 12-15 fps posterized motion): push-in 12, pan 19 (one 223px/360 pan), pull-out 4, drift 9; zoom range 0.57-1.63, median peak at 0.41 so easing is near-symmetric
why_it_works: low-fps stepped camera gives a hand-animated/archival feel and hides AI-image softness
use_when: static still or generated image must carry 2-3 s

finding: Tiny serif caption (about 3-4% of frame height, high-contrast Didone-like, italic for the key word: 'Build a wall.', 'the port.', 'colony') placed dead centre or on a quiet area (sky, water, wall), phrase-by-phrase so a sentence is revealed in 2-3 successive chunks over the same picture
why_it_works: small centered type over a calm region never fights the image; italic on one word is the only emphasis needed

finding: Whole film graded to one desaturated sepia/greyscale world with a single colour accent per beat (red coat of the English soldier, red palisade stakes, orange map highlight, gold coins); cream paper cards have vignette, fibre noise and visible horizontal scanlines
why_it_works: colour only where the story point is; scanlines/grain glue AI images and paper cards into one surface
use_when: mixed-source images need a common look; point the eye at the plot object

finding: A single full-body figure (governor on wooden leg) is cut from his scene and re-placed in the same street without outline or shadow edge, in colour on a greyscale street; small scale (about 25% frame height) with the street dominating
why_it_works: selective colour makes cut-out read as 'the subject' without needing a border
use_when: introducing a named person in a place

finding: Scene-to-scene transitions are hard cuts on the beat of the sentence; map shots use pull-out zoom ending on a tinted overlay (red wash over relief map, orange over town plan) to show the thing the line talks about
why_it_works: colour overlay animates the map without moving geometry
use_when: line names a region, territory, route

finding: Mixed-media story: B&W stills/footage, parchment cards, wood-grain desk with props (comic covers, banknotes) and flat sky/map backdrops; each is full-bleed 9:16 and one object-focus per beat; props on the wood desk are drawn at ~45% frame width and tilted 5-10 deg with stacked overlap
why_it_works: desk-top tabletop view makes objects tactile and gives a neutral stage for cut-out objects
use_when: the story names a physical thing (cover, money, letter)

finding: Banknotes enter the desk scene one by one: each bill drops onto the comic cover with slight rotation (3 notes in ~1 s), then the stack shrinks and slides toward the bottom-right as the text says 'kept everything'
why_it_works: literal piece-by-piece entry mirrors the sentence count
use_when: an amount or accumulation is narrated

finding: Parchment cards used as chapter beats ('It's 1932.', 'Jerry is small, shy.', 'In 1938.'): plain textured paper, centered italic line, 0.9-1.5 s, always cut into a photo with the next line already on it
why_it_works: establishes time/state cleanly and makes the photo cut feel like a page turn

finding: Caption set in white italic serif with soft outer glow over dark footage and in black italic on paper; placed on the subject's torso/low-contrast area; words appear in chunks of 2-4 words, replacing in place
why_it_works: glow keeps legibility on mixed photo without a box; chunk replacement is a text 'cut' on the same beat as voice

finding: Mostly pans (24) and pull-outs (11) at slow speed with the move fastest early (median peak_at 0.12, i.e. ease-out); only 4 shots stepped, so motion is smooth, zoom 0.63-1.21
why_it_works: ease-out into a still frame lets the viewer read the caption on a settled picture
use_when: footage needs a gentle move that settles

finding: Longest soft transition (44.8-47.6 s) is a dissolve from handshake photo to a sky/city flyover with a hero figure; ends on a hard cut to portrait of a man (talking head) for the sign-off
why_it_works: one long dissolve is reserved for the payoff, everything else cuts

style: B&W footage, parchment and wood desk

finding: Open on a dark wood desk seen from above: book covers (about 40% frame width, soft drop shadow, slight tilt) enter one after another, then a tall stack of spines fills the left edge while the caption wraps down the right in a column of 1-2 words per line
why_it_works: top-down wood desk = neutral tactile stage; object stack gives scale (many books) and negative space for the text column
use_when: opening hook about a product/book/object category

finding: Newspaper front pages enter as tilted flat sheets that slide and overlap in a quick 4-5 sheet stack (each ~0.3-0.5 s), with headline words highlighted by a neon-yellow marker block; the sheet scale grows until the masthead fills the frame
why_it_works: stacking pages conveys volume of the press; yellow marker is the single loud accent over grey print
use_when: a claim is about headlines or documents

finding: Grey crumpled-paper cards ('sell papers.', 'Nobody believes in.', 'No scandals.', 'Just the news.') between B&W portrait/footage shots; the card holds 0.8-1.2 s and text swaps in place (3 chunks) without a cut, then cuts to the next photo
why_it_works: light grey paper is the rest beat; in-place text swap = micro-cut with no picture event
use_when: a rhythmic list of short claims

finding: Object-as-metaphor on the desk: a newspaper with three copper coins lies at an angle, a coin slides off (3 cents to 1 cent) in sync with 'from three cents to one cent'; the paper first peels in from the corner (page-curl reveal) of the previous front page
why_it_works: the picture performs the number; curl reveal is a paper-native transition

finding: 19 of 45 shots are holds and 30 of 45 stepped; holds sit on the desk and paper cards, motion is spent on archival footage. Max shot 4.5 s, ASL 1.23 s
why_it_works: static desk compositions give text time; stepped motion on footage keeps it vintage

finding: Same serif face in sizes by role: tiny caption centered on photos, large 4-line column on the wood desk, and masthead-scale newsprint inside images; italics rarely used; white on dark, near-black on paper
why_it_works: one family keeps film coherent; size is set by free space, not by importance

finding: Cut-out business figures (full body, hard white-fringe-free edges) sit centred on a white/grey 'Wall Street Journal' newsprint ghost background at about 25-30% frame height, with desk, computer and props as separate cut-out layers, leaving 60% empty paper
why_it_works: lots of paper negative space isolates the character like a magazine cutout
use_when: introducing a person at a desk or role

finding: Lower-third-style label: white serif text on a solid royal-blue rectangle highlight (marker-block) behind key words, appearing word by word ('never', 'Larry Fink', 'adding billions'); blue block doubles as name tag
why_it_works: one flat accent colour for emphasis keeps the greyscale scene readable
use_when: naming a person or the key number

finding: Photo cut-outs of people (two-by-six) pop onto a flat cyan field in a staggered row of different heights with white borders, each stepping in ~0.2 s, to illustrate 'seven partners'; banknote stack photo sits on newsprint with a blue label above
why_it_works: count is shown by count; flat colour field separates cut-outs from archival grey

finding: World map in pale blue on newsprint with countries tinted red one at a time (US, China) while text reads on, and a hero portrait on a split red/blue panel with a logo plate behind head, small plane flying across
why_it_works: colour fill on a simplified map = quick geography fact; hero panel gives portrait a poster look

finding: Paper ghost-newsprint cards bridge footage clips; 10 soft transitions (0.4-1.3 s) mainly fades through the paper. Hard cuts between TV-footage clips of Fink with a bottom ticker (real broadcast chyrons) left in
why_it_works: footage cuts hard, graphics dissolve; broadcast chyron adds authenticity

finding: Opening title treatment: dark poster with a stylised boxing illustration and huge white serif 'ROCKY'; counter numbers ($185, $222, $225 Million) drop in on a white placard that stacks upward, each replacing the last within 0.4 s
why_it_works: number ticking up on the same placard shows growth in place

finding: Colour footage kept full-bleed, with an outline-yellow New Jersey map shape (flat yellow with black outline) laid on top of boxing frame to place the location; text arcs in a single italic line near the middle
why_it_works: flat graphic over live-action shows place without cutting away

finding: Green cutting-mat desk (top-down): photo prints taped with paper tape, handwritten notes and polaroids slide in one by one and a red photo-corner; ends with a mid-shot of an executive in a seated cut-out and then a red envelope that opens (flap lifts, letter slides up) with 'one condition' text
why_it_works: physical scrapbook props make a paper world; envelope reveal is a built-in suspense beat

finding: Photo stills are given a slow push-in with posterised stepping (33 of 46 shots), type swaps in place per phrase (2-4 words); 17 drift shots on photos of Stallone/dog keep the face off-centre so the caption sits beside it
why_it_works: face stays inside upper-thirds while caption occupies the lower or side area

finding: Climax is a hard cut from the hero silhouette (arms raised, big 'Rocky.' type) to a newspaper front page scaled in: 'Made $225 million' headline slides up from the bottom; no dissolve
why_it_works: newsprint headline is the receipt for the story

finding: Rhythm is uneven: long 5.9 s hold on a hero image while the line is spoken, then 3-5 sub-second flicks (dog photos, fighters). ASL 1.27, 7.7 events per 10 s
why_it_works: burst-hold contrast keeps retention

finding: B&W archival portraits/footage full-bleed, with warm cream floral-paper cards as chapter breaks and a dark wood desk for object beats (torn lined notebook page, index cards, printed paper). Text sits in the dark mid-tones of the photo (chest, suit) never on faces
why_it_works: three grounds (photo, paper, wood) rotate so no ground lasts more than ~6 s
use_when: a 50 s story with many different beats

finding: Index cards with handwriting and waveform scribbles enter onto a black ground one after another with a drop shadow, each tilted differently (5-15 deg), hands placing them; caption words are lifted to the card edges and orbit the pile (every message, every image, every sound)
why_it_works: physical hands set cards: places pieces in a human act; words around the pile read as labels

finding: A torn-edge scanned paper (academic paper page) lands on cream card, then on wood desk the page slides to centre and zooms to its title block; text on a paper card changes from 'Then' to 'Then in 1948' by chunks
why_it_works: paper object on paper ground, tilt and torn edge sells it as real

finding: Match-by-subject cuts: radio/phone portrait to next portrait (Roosevelt phone, Churchill phone) on the same phone prop; ocean wave to new scene; footage jump-cut within 0.5 s of the voice; 9 soft transitions at 0.4-2.5 s used for time jumps ('Today')
why_it_works: same prop across two shots reads as one idea; soft only for time jumps

finding: Caption set in white small italic serif with glow on photo, and black on cream; occasionally a black censor-bar strike behind a word (redacted-document gag) at the intro of the war message
why_it_works: typography speaks the era: redaction bar = wartime secrecy

style: B&W archive, index cards, wood desk

finding: Pure found-footage essay: talking-head interview clips (BBC, podcasts, Rogan, Davos) in B&W or desaturated, full-bleed, subject offset and caption in a single line at the lower third in tiny white serif; no cut-outs at all
why_it_works: consistent desaturation makes 20 sources look like one film; tiny caption never covers face

finding: Stat beat: giant sans numbers (42,656 / 81,109 / 97,000 layoffs) cropped by the frame, background of faded news text; the number steps up three times in 1 s; punch-in to a cropped zoomed headline
why_it_works: cropped oversized numerals feel big and the ticking count reads as growth

finding: Text-only cards: near-black ground, one tiny line centred; text swaps in place as the claim flips ('very good at predicting what technology destroys' then 'terrible at predicting what it creates'), no picture event
why_it_works: the pure type card is a thesis moment; the flip is shown by swapping words, not by cutting

finding: Fastest montage runs 8-12 clips in 4-5 s (celebrity/podcast faces, 0.3 s each, posterize-glitch at 0.14 s) before a 6 s hold on one speaker; 50 of 95 shots drift, 24 hold; ASL 1.02
why_it_works: burst then hold; speed carries 'everyone says this', hold carries the argument

finding: Glitch/datamosh flash of 0.13-0.2 s (one frame of RGB-split and smear) at clip changes; 30 soft_transitions are all 1-frame glitches (0.14 s), plus long 1 s cross-dissolves in the 40-50 s span
why_it_works: a 4-frame glitch marks a cut without delaying the narration

finding: A laptop-on-black-desk framing: the speaker video plays inside a laptop screen (about 60% frame width) in a pure black room, then the screen fills the frame, then back to plain talking head; captions ride at screen bottom
why_it_works: frame-in-frame signals 'recorded on a screen' and the black room gives full contrast; zoom to full-bleed escalates intensity

finding: Article headlines are shown as live typography (huge serif headline, 4 lines, tight leading), then a phone mock-up slides in over the headline with a TikTok video playing in it, then replaced by a second phone clip; screenshots of tweets on cream paper with yellow marker highlight on the key phrase
why_it_works: layering device-in-front-of-text says 'what people say online'; yellow marker names the key claim

finding: Slowest of the set on cuts: 36 of 56 shots are holds, max shot 9.25 s, ASL 1.47; all energy comes from caption chunks changing every ~0.5 s over a held face
why_it_works: on a talking head the caption is the motion

finding: Ending cards: dark then white full-frame cards with a single tiny centred line fading in by chunks (three chunks across 5 s); final card flips from near-black to white to land the hopeful turn
why_it_works: dark-to-white flip carries the mood change with no image

finding: Caption over a moving talking head (zoomed laptop) is tiny and low-contrast against the dark face; this is the weak spot, while the better pieces put it on a plain band or glow it
why_it_works: n/a (anti-pattern)
use_when: avoid: caption over face in motion

style: talking heads, phone mocks, tweet cards

finding: Yellow highlighter block behind a name ('Michael Collins') as a label on a portrait, plus a dashed yellow line tracing a 240,000-mile path from Earth to the moon module and a dashed yellow circle ringing a tiny capsule; yellow is the only graphic colour over NASA footage
why_it_works: one hand-drawn-looking accent identifies the subject in archival footage without cutting away
use_when: point to a small thing in archive footage

finding: Scale diagram on black: real moon photo (about 60% frame width) with a tiny yellow dot as the 'dot behind' and a cut-out lander that crosses from the left, moon rising from the bottom edge as the yellow dot grows to a disc; camera pulls out so size ratios show
why_it_works: a sparse black ground, 3 objects, and one animated size ratio explain isolation

finding: Window-vignette: archive images appear as a small soft-glow rectangle floating in black (about 30% width), then expand to full-bleed in 0.3 s; used when the line shifts from the lander to the view from the orbit
why_it_works: window-in-black is an iris-style reveal that resets the eye

finding: Footage is slowly punched in with up to x2.8 scale on the face of a man at a lectern; 8 rotates and 8 push-ins give a restless feel; ASL 1.28 s with 14 soft transitions (0.4-1.3 s)
why_it_works: digital zoom on low-res archive creates attention without new material

finding: Grade kept natural: dark space and grey lunar surface are the neutrals, warm 60s film colour on interviews; captions small white serif with soft glow; no paper or texture layer here
why_it_works: space footage is already high-contrast; adding paper would hurt

finding: Ultra-fast photo-stack montage: 48 events in 12 s (ASL 0.25 s, 39 events per 10 s), alternating a huge serif word on a light-grey card (Future / wasn't / clear / then. / It / isn't / now / Keep building.) with a collage of 2-4 photos of founders stacked at different tilts; each word about 0.3 s, photos 0.2-0.5 s
why_it_works: one word per beat sets the tempo; the photo pile is the proof; it only works because the words are huge and the message is short
use_when: a tagline/trailer sting at the end of a piece

finding: Words in a condensed, heavy-contrast serif at about 40-55% of frame height, dark grey on light-grey vignette card with slight inner shadow; final line 'Keep building.' is smaller and holds 1.5 s
why_it_works: size contrast between the single huge words and the final smaller line signals 'the end'
use_when: kinetic type with a closing line

finding: Photo collages: 2-4 photos layered on a black ground with light-grey sheets peeking behind, offset (never centred), each photo about 50-70% of frame width, tilted <5 deg; the subject faces sit in the upper half
why_it_works: offset edges of stacked prints give depth with no extra elements

finding: No camera move (zoom 1.0-1.03; 29 holds, 19 tiny drifts): all motion is the swap itself; each photo stack arrives with a short slide-snap of ~2 frames
why_it_works: at 0.25 s per event any camera move would blur; the cut is the move

finding: Black scrapbook ground with a pile of ephemera: red Coca-Cola can, tickets (stub 'specimen' cards), stamps, polaroid, dotted trajectory lines, notebook with spiral, tape and small coins; items are separate cut-outs with paper-white edge and soft shadow, overlapping at different tilts and the caption text rides on top in white serif sentences
why_it_works: dark ground makes every colourful prop pop; overlap and shadow give a physical layered pile; props relate to the story (cards, can, coins)

finding: Pattern: archive photo shot (2-3 s) then cream paper card with 3-5 word line (1-1.5 s) then props collage (3 s), repeated; 27 of 76 shots are holds, 42 stepped; ASL 0.86, 11.4 events per 10 s
why_it_works: three-ground rotation (photo, paper, black collage) keeps variety while the voice drives
use_when: story with a clear thesis line

finding: Establishing vintage illustration: blimp slides across sky with yellow marker year '1949' (marker block left behind it), then the camera tilts up to the skyline and 'New York City' fades in as big sepia serif; each element has its own entry in sequence
why_it_works: year and place enter separately: two facts, two beats

finding: A pocket menu (yellow card) enters and unfolds with a red can and a framed portrait pinned over it; later a collage of storefront photos on a pink gingham tablecloth with paper tape corners, each photo dropping in with a 3-5 deg tilt
why_it_works: different grounds (gingham, wood, black) signal chapter changes within the same world

finding: Sepia B&W figure photos, with spot colour only in props (red, yellow, blue ticket stripe); paper cards are warm grey with fibre noise; text white on black, dark on paper
why_it_works: restricted palette so the props carry the colour

finding: Pan 29, pull-out 15, push-in 13 on single images; peak speed early (median 0.2) and a few punch-ins to zoom x2.9 on the card reader / ticket detail
why_it_works: punch to a detail on the line that names it
use_when: naming an object in a composed layout

finding: Anime clips full-bleed inside a CRT frame over a wall of wanted posters (purple/blue frame), a character silhouette from behind watching 'To be continued' on a screen, then cut to B&W creator footage with one yellow-tinted element (hair/cap); manga covers as paper props on a wood desk; flat white timeline card with a dated icon (1997, 1998 Google logo) sliding on a line
why_it_works: each ground fits the beat: TV for the show, desk for the book, white timeline for dates

finding: Manga pages as paper props on a wood desk: two or three pages slide in staggered from different sides, overlapping with 3-8 deg tilts and soft shadow; then a mirrored/kaleidoscope grid of characters fills the frame behind a text line
why_it_works: printed pages on wood desk is the repeated 'object stage' of this studio

finding: Article headline screenshot (white page, orange highlight over the key phrase) overlaid on a stack of manga volumes at the bottom, then an ink-style yellowed parchment spread with a figure; the screenshot is cropped so the highlight is in the optical centre
why_it_works: web screenshot with a highlight stands as the evidence beat

finding: 36 of 76 shots are holds, 33 stepped; max 7.25 s on a scrolling article, ASL 0.94 (10.5 events per 10 s); stepping motion on anime stills mimics animation on twos
why_it_works: fast cuts on drawn material, slow hold on reading material

finding: Caption over anime sits in small white serif near the bottom or centre with glow; mirrored double-print on the symmetrical frame is a type-free graphic beat; headline text is real article typography, not set by the studio
why_it_works: keeps caption quiet against saturated art

finding: Every caption chunk sits on a solid neon-yellow label rectangle (black serif, about 3% cap height, tight padding 6 px horizontally), centred on the subject's torso, hands or the horizon; the label replaces in place every ~0.4 s with 2-4 words; when a word is stressed ('Beaten.', 'Starved.') the label holds alone
why_it_works: yellow label is readable on any grey engraving and its centre placement becomes a fixed eye anchor so the viewer never searches for text
use_when: single-colour (greyscale) image world; need guaranteed legibility

finding: Whole film is greyscale engravings with a chromatic-aberration fringe (red/blue edges) and film grain; only yellow is ever coloured: a violin cut-out, yellow chain band on ankles and neck, a yellow coin, a yellow disc over a head, a yellow crowd tint
why_it_works: the yellow object IS the plot noun, so colour carries meaning and ties to the label colour

finding: Yellow cut-out props slide in over engravings: violin enters from the right edge and grows x1.6 behind a person, chains animate as yellow arcs drawn on a wrist; a yellow vertical bar drops from the top to show the chain to a wall
why_it_works: a flat colour prop on grey photo needs no shadow; it looks like marker pen
use_when: illustrate an object the line mentions on an old print

finding: 79 events in 50 s (ASL 0.64, 15.5 per 10 s): 40 holds, 28 stepped, max 2.9 s; each engraving is used for 1-2 label swaps then replaced; paper-grey cards with 'It took another / 1830 / 1852' count a timeline in 3 swaps
why_it_works: label swaps keep movement even on holds

finding: Text-wall transition: a dense grey paragraph ('Beaten. Starved...') fades in as a background texture, scrolls up while the headline words ('London's only asylum') appear in white above it, then cuts to an engraving
why_it_works: the wall of words is the 'document' beat made from type

finding: Engravings pushed in or panned up at 12 fps stepped; punch to detail (foot in shackle) at x2+ for one label; peak speed near start (median 0.06) so the image settles for the read
why_it_works: quick ease-out settles the picture before the caption

finding: Pale grey paper ground with faint column or building ghost watermark (Corinthian column, bank facade) behind text-only cards; cut-out objects (Federal Reserve facade, Bank of America tower, train car, island map) float on the grey as hard-edged cut-outs with a drop shadow, no frame
why_it_works: light neutral ground lets any B&W photo cut-out sit without a border; ghost watermark gives depth to empty cards

finding: Portrait grid assembly: first man pops in alone with a yellow name label, then five more portraits appear around him in two rows (each a small snap, about 0.3 s apart), then a newspaper sheet slides up over them
why_it_works: build-up of the group portrait by count; paper sheet then covers it to move on

finding: Map cut-out (island) on paper with a yellow cone spot-light line to an inset photo circle; geographic anchor + detail photo in a round mask
why_it_works: leader line plus round inset is the classic atlas callout

finding: Longest and slowest in the set: 29 shots over 66 s, ASL 2.29, max shot 11.25 s on a held collage; 21 pans; text-only cards of 1.5-3 s ('For nine days.', 'through the banks.')
why_it_works: slower pacing suits an institutional/serious story

finding: Two caption modes: small italic text directly on photos (white, lower third, no label) and bold yellow serif for the key proper noun ('New Jersey', 'Institution', 'Federal Reserve' on a yellow plaque above the facade)
why_it_works: proper noun gets the accent; the rest stays quiet
use_when: one key proper noun per scene

finding: Federal Reserve building changes by cut-out stacking: facade slides in, yellow plaque drops on top, then gavel, coins and a red-roof house pile up beside it as a symbolic cluster, each item 0.3 s
why_it_works: icons accumulate to state a concept (power) without a sentence

finding: Two caption registers: tiny cursive script (handwriting font, white, sometimes rotated along the image) for names and mood lines, and the small serif for facts; names appear as a 'name plate' under the person (UNITED KINGDOM / USA flag plate with yellow underline) lifted from the real conference placards
why_it_works: script plus serif separates the narrator's aside from fact; real placards double as the lower third

finding: Colour appears only as accents on greyscale archive: red blotch/blood dots over a beach scene, a yellow halo ring behind a head (x1.2 growing circle), black plane silhouettes crossing the sky with a script '4 years of war'; page ground is a cream diamond-pattern paper for the money section
why_it_works: a drawn mark (halo, blotch) on the photo points at the person or injury
use_when: mark a person in a group archive photo

finding: Currency notes are cut-outs that appear on cream paper in sequence: one green note alone, then a spread of 6-8 foreign notes and a coin, each placed at a different tilt, then they all disappear and a single dollar bill scales to the centre ('America wanted the dollar at the centre')
why_it_works: clutter of many versus one dominant item is the argument made visually

finding: Slow pan or push-in across archive (24 pans, 29 stepped), with the camera starting on an empty part of the image and drifting to the subject while text appears; start frame often a room view, finishing on the person
why_it_works: camera move doubles as reveal of the subject

finding: ASL 1.48 (6.6 events per 10 s), max shot 7.8 s on a paper card of money; intercuts of portrait (2-3 s) with a text-only white card ('no money') for 1 s
why_it_works: a stark white card on 'no money' gives the line weight

style: archive plus script captions, cream money

finding: Landscape 16:9 gangster story at 86 events in 41 s (ASL 0.48, 20.8 per 10 s, 55 holds, max 2.3 s); every 0.3-0.5 s the picture or the type changes, with extreme close-ups (eye, mouth, hat) and flashing white frames between
why_it_works: a thriller register: speed is the style; holds are on text only

finding: Browser-window collage: small blue-title-bar windows containing crops of one face (eye, mouth, hat) arranged and rotated around the frame, popping in staggered with the caption 'is across the table' placed beside; red blood-splatter mask paints over a mugshot as the line says 'killed'
why_it_works: UI window crops cut one face into parts for a 'surveillance' feel; red splatter is a single-colour shock

finding: Type changes size and weight mid-sentence (heavy sans 'IMAGINE' with the letters at varying sizes; thin captions; 'No Boss Of All Bosses' as a staggered list of words in black on white blocks over a tilted photo; signature script 'Charlie Luciano' on torn paper)
why_it_works: type shape does the work; the signature on torn paper acts as ID

finding: Black-and-white with deep black vignettes; strong light shaft and silhouette (horse rider, empty throne with cash heap) fill the frame; the throne scene pushes in and then shatters into coins; palette limited to B&W + blood red + one blue (Silicon Valley sign)
why_it_works: high-contrast greyscale hides generated-image artefacts; the colour hit lands on the key moment

finding: The film ends by cutting hard to a sky-blue background with a green freeway sign (Silicon Valley) and real talking-head interviews, so the genre jumps from mob drama to tech; separate 0.5 s zoom-blur between photos with radial motion blur
why_it_works: colour jump signals thesis change

finding: Mixed maker documentary: a 3D-render toaster exploded into parts on a white studio ground, then real footage of a man mining ore, with tiny captions in white serif placed by word over the action (mine the ore / smelt the iron); flip-clock date cards (FEBRUARY 17 / JUNE 30) bridge time jumps
why_it_works: clean white product ground vs dark workshop footage makes two registers; flip-clock card gives time at a glance

finding: Huge outline-less condensed words flash full-frame (Toaster, BUILD IT., 'that's the point', 'TWO YEARS') while tiny captions run elsewhere; big words are blurred or smeared by motion on the way out
why_it_works: scale jump from tiny to giant creates a thesis beat

finding: Photo wall: dozens of small portraits tile into a curved 3D grid (fisheye bend), the camera flies through, and a few faces pop out larger; later portraits float in dark space at different depths with a slow drift and fisheye warp
why_it_works: crowd of faces shows 'many people'; fisheye gives parallax without a 3D scene

finding: 92 events in 51 s (ASL 0.56, 17.8 per 10 s); the 13 soft transitions are 0.13 s flashes (white or glow burn-through) at clip changes; each caption word has a 0.2 s soft glow in
why_it_works: white flash hides the cut and keeps rhythm

finding: All shots have a move: 35 drift, 22 pull-out, 20 pan, 13 push-in, 10 rotate; peak at the very start (median 0.07) so each shot lands as a snap then eases
why_it_works: ease-out start makes cuts feel punchy

style: white studio, dark footage, flash cuts

finding: 16:9 business-news essay at 146 events in 72 s (ASL 0.49, 20 per 10 s, 36 holds, max 2.3 s); alternates cinematic stock/real footage with text-only black cards and numeric cards ($5 / $3 billion / $2.4 Billion / 40 people) that each last 0.4-1 s
why_it_works: numbers each get their own beat, so the story of a deal reads as a count-down

finding: Strobe flashes: 30 soft transitions are each one 0.13-0.17 s frame of white or glow (5 in a row at 59-60 s), used between clips and inside number counts; no dissolve over 0.2 s except a few long ones
why_it_works: 1-frame flash hides cut and adds impact

finding: Screenshots in the story are treated as props: a news headline blown up and cropped so a highlight (black block with white text) sits on the key clause ('$600 million less'), then the layout zooms in; money and numbers rendered as large serif over a dark teal-tinted stock of banknotes
why_it_works: zoom into one highlighted clause is the quote beat

finding: Caption words appear as small white serif over footage with soft glow; number and key labels are 5-10x larger serif; names of companies are shown as their real logos fading in (Windsurf, ChatGPT mark, Google search box zoomed in circular lens)
why_it_works: two sizes only: caption and hero
use_when: video mixing narration and key numbers

finding: Photo cluster: portrait photos on white or black float as a tilted pile that pushes in slowly; a lens-circle mask (Google search page seen through a circle) zooms from the bar to the whole page
why_it_works: circular mask is a magnifier: points at the one detail

finding: A retro TV set (CRT with static then the face) as the frame for the talking head, then the footage breaks out to full-bleed with a blurred background and a lens glow; later the person is shown as a negative-colour inverted photo for a 0.5 s flash
why_it_works: CRT frame starts the story in the past; inversion flash marks a jump in tone

finding: Check/cheque prop on a wooden desk with a dim amber light: '$1.7 billion' text engraved onto the desk, the cheque slides in and a 'check' word hits; then the Uber logo on white shatters into cracks
why_it_works: prop plus sound-of-money word gives the metaphor a body; crack effect shows collapse

finding: Huge serif word (turning) pushes full-frame then shrinks to a normal caption on a phone UI mock; ride-hail UI screenshots in white; year cards '2016', '2017', '8 years' are centred serif on white with a vertical blur wipe between them
why_it_works: year cards on white give a clean time marker between dense clips

finding: A robotic hand passing a bundle of notes on white; the notes then multiply, stack and drift down the frame as dozens of copies with a gray label 'And with $1.5 billion' - a tile/repeat entrance for scale
why_it_works: repetition shows a vast sum without a number

finding: ASL 0.9; one 8.6 s hold on an in-car clip (Bloomberg-style) with the caption changing every 0.6 s while the footage plays; the rest cuts every 0.5-1 s
why_it_works: found footage holds when it is itself the evidence

style: CRT frame, white cards, cash props

finding: Game explainer in portrait: Minecraft house with a 3D-rendered label (pixel plaque) where captions sit as blue pixel-label strips tracking the character, then real game footage of other titles; a flat white card with faint graph-paper pattern for abstract lines; software UI screenshots (forum post) with pointer cursor animating
why_it_works: the medium's own visual language (pixel label, cursor) styles the captions; white graph-paper card is the neutral break

finding: Match cut by subject: from Minecraft builds (house, castle, skyline) to GTA and Mario via one build-up of '8-bit' scenes; pixel-glitch bars at the cut; 15 soft transitions 0.4-1.4 s
why_it_works: each game is a new rung in a ladder of what's possible
use_when: series of examples in the same genre

finding: Small serif captions placed on the sky or sparse ground in game scenes; achievement toast ('Advancement Made!') real from the game used as an overlay at 15% width; an arrow doodle line with label 'replica of the Eiffel Tower'
why_it_works: empty sky area carries text without a box

finding: ASL 1.1 (8.9 events per 10 s), 19 holds and 20 drifts; no stepped motion; 5.6 s max
why_it_works: medium-paced for a tutorial-style argument

style: game footage, pixel labels, UI shots

finding: Cool-grey paper ground with halftone and torn-edge portrait cut-outs; a black-and-white portrait torn out of a paper strip enters from the bottom; the finance story layers handwritten maths scribbles (a+b)^2, geometry diagrams, a line chart and halftone dot patterns as backgrounds to a subject
why_it_works: the ground itself describes the subject (equations, charts) so no extra props are needed

finding: Redacted-document typography: a block of alphabet lines (Aa Bb ... Zz) with black censor bars over lines, and words 'He cracked Soviet codes' revealed through the gaps in red-orange; NSA seal fades in over the paper
why_it_works: redaction bars make secrecy a visible texture; red words are the only accent

finding: Portrait stack builds by snaps: small framed photo of one man at centre, then three more portraits pop in around him at different sizes (each ~0.25 s) with big serif text 'and code breakers' crossing over them, then all collapse back to one frame; 2-3 px glitch smear on the slide
why_it_works: build-up count equals the 'team' being named; return to a single frame re-centres

finding: Typewritten 'TOP SECRET' memo scans: an employee performance review page enlarged to full frame with a CONFIDENTIAL stamp and signature, then a circular portrait crop with a green square-grid growth chart appearing around it ('66% annual returns')
why_it_works: fake-real documents deliver 'proof'; circular crop with a graph ties face to number
use_when: a figure attached to a person

finding: 30 holds, 26 stepped, ASL 0.99 (10 per 10 s); the big beats (Nobel medal, a team group photo) hold ~3 s with yellow circle or line accent drawn over a face
why_it_works: the yellow ring picks the person out of a group shot
use_when: identify a person in a group

finding: Fastest piece of the batch: 76 events in 14 s (ASL 0.18, 53 per 10 s), max shot 0.77 s; ultra-cropped thumbnails (a small rectangular window of video, 30-50% of frame) float over a flat white, black or print-texture ground, and each window changes every 2-4 frames
why_it_works: small windows on a flat ground read as a collage sheet; speed is hidden by the stable ground
use_when: a brand-reel teaser of a person/company

finding: Window-on-ground: clip rectangles (about 40% frame width) layered at several depths on dollar-bill close-up, halftone dots, black field or white page; there are 3-5 overlapping rectangles with hard edges, no shadow, each different size; inverted high-contrast portrait cut-out and a Michelangelo hands crop
why_it_works: mixed scale windows give a collage depth with no animation; inversion and halftone make unrelated footage cohere

finding: Type is graphic: giant cropped black letters (partially visible words) with a small image inside, a digit counter ($919,298 counting) over a ghosted figure, a word-card 'READY' with a cursor block, website heading 'Space' at top-left; type is mostly bold grotesque rather than the serif of other pieces
why_it_works: cropped giant letters give a poster feel in a 0.4 s window

finding: 4 flashes (0.13-0.16 s) only; every other cut is hard on the beat; cuts go between match shapes (eye to a logo plate across eyes, drone to rocket)
why_it_works: shape-match makes a 3-frame shot readable

finding: Envelope reveal: a cream envelope sits on black, 4-5 archive photos spring out of it fanned (slide up and rotate ~5 deg each, 0.1 s apart) and the front photo is picked with a yellow label ('Walter Freeman'); the same envelope idea returns later as pages
why_it_works: the envelope is a container that opens the story and gives a cast reveal
use_when: introducing a person from the archive

finding: Surgical tray top-down on steel: instruments (reflex hammer, pick) laid out on a tray at 40% frame width with a drop shadow, entering one by one; text sits above the tray in the clean metal area
why_it_works: object stage in the right material for the topic (steel tray) with space above for text

finding: Circle-crop multiplication: one round-masked photo detail appears in the middle of black, then it replicates into a grid of 4x5 small copies in 1 s; later one eye from a portrait appears in a slit with a light ray
why_it_works: repetition suggests a procedure carried out many times

finding: Top-down road shot: white car dots moving along a black road, the camera pans along the road to show a building, a bus, wood grid; the arc shows the van's route 'across America' from above, caption small italic beside the road
why_it_works: abstract aerial view carries the line 'drove across America' with no travel footage
use_when: journey or spread of an idea

finding: Dark charcoal ground with film grain, almost entirely B&W; accents are a yellow label (name), red dots on an X-ray head and a green neon LOBOTOMOBILE sign; vintage family photos in colour come only at the end for the emotional beat
why_it_works: colour saved for the human payoff so it reads emotionally

finding: 26 soft transitions of 0.4-1.3 s (fades between archive clips) while text swaps by phrase; hard cuts for clinical footage
why_it_works: fades soften the grim clips

style: dark archive, envelope reveal, circle grid

finding: Landscape wood-desk opening: polaroid-style photos with a thin white border laid on the wood at 3-5 deg tilt, linked by a thin white connector line to small labels and a watch-with-paper (document) prop; the desk returns as the background of text cards ('in Hollywood,' in white serif over wood)
why_it_works: white line plus small label is a clean who-is-who without boxes; wood ground works as both prop table and text card

finding: Auction price counts in on live footage: '$' then '$17.' then '$17.8 million.' typed in large white serif across the lower-middle of the auctioneer shot, each step 0.3 s
why_it_works: the number lands as the gavel/crowd sound hits; big type over a calm area

finding: Repeated phrase swap card on a dark ground: a watch crop on the right and text on the left, with 'The same watch.' set in upright then italic serif ('Always on his wrist.', 'his wrist.' in italic) - upright for the base clause, italic for the payoff clause
why_it_works: upright to italic marks the emotional turn inside a single line

finding: Dark charcoal text cards ('No ceremony.', 'No explanation.') between photo spreads; year cards ('1968', '1984', 'In 2017') in large serif directly over footage with the clip dimmed 40%
why_it_works: year over dimmed footage keeps motion alive while stating time

finding: ASL 0.73, 13.5 events per 10 s; 36 holds, 28 drifts; B&W vs colour footage alternate (colour for Newman racing, B&W for family), with red thin underline marks (a red line pointing at a face in a family photo)
why_it_works: colour/B&W split signals public vs private

finding: 153 events in 84 s (ASL 0.55, 18 per 10 s); every 2-4 words a new shot, with a 0.13-0.2 s flash (white-glow) every ~2 s; longest shot 9.2 s is the climax card ('2008' tickers)
why_it_works: one clip per phrase; a hold only at the climax

finding: Words glow: small white serif with a bloom/halo, bigger italic script words ('feel lucky', 'made the') at about 20% of frame height on pure black; number cards (16, 65, 65 billion, 2008) appear with the numeral lighting up and bloom, each 0.5-1.2 s
why_it_works: glow stays readable on any footage and makes black cards feel lit

finding: Photo grids and walls: a 3x4 mosaic of faces of victims or investors, a tilted wall of portraits at 3D angles, a fan of 5 photos around a headline; UI states (APPROVED / REJECTED / PENDING) wrap in a rotating cylinder of text
why_it_works: grid of faces gives 'the many'; the cylinder of repeating words gives a bureaucratic feel

finding: Match by motion: hand with banknotes enters, then banknote texture fills the frame and becomes the new background (macro of a note's portrait); zoom through a logo (JPMorgan, Nasdaq) into the building; 74 drifts with radial zoom blur at each cut
why_it_works: object-to-texture zoom makes the cut seamless
use_when: jump from an object to a larger context

finding: Teal-and-orange cinema grade on stock footage, with blacks crushed and vignette; the only graphics are white text and the occasional red (blood or alert) tint; no paper at all
why_it_works: one grade makes stock footage from dozens of sources one film

finding: Satellite street map as the stage: a top-down aerial photo of one block with small cut-out props (shop signs, storefront photos with white border, polaroid portrait) pinned onto it at 4-8 deg tilts, red thread lines connecting a portrait polaroid to four shop signs on a wood desk
why_it_works: map + pinned props + red thread is a detective board; it explains ownership connections without a diagram
use_when: showing relations between people and places

finding: Logo cut-outs (Nvidia, AWS, Google Cloud, OpenAI, Anthropic) land one by one on the same aerial street map, each in an irregular photo shape with a pixel-blur placeholder on the neighbour; the map camera drifts so the logos slide with parallax
why_it_works: reusing the same map ground ties 'real estate' to 'AI hardware'
use_when: metaphor carried across the whole film

finding: Alternates three registers: tiny serif lines on footage, big glowing italics on black ('except', 'that's it'), and numeric hero ('80%') at 35% frame height over a blurred hardware shot
why_it_works: size jumps mark thesis and numbers

finding: 123 events in 57 s (ASL 0.46, 21.5 per 10 s), max 2.4 s; zoom range 0.21-1.54 (a quick pull-out from a detail to the planet); 61 drifts and 23 pull-outs
why_it_works: scale-zoom from a block to the Earth is the argument's shape
use_when: scale jump from local to global

finding: Closing montage swaps to white-ground photo collages (portraits with soft shadow, 3 tilted photos offset in the frame) after 50 s of dark footage; the white ground marks the payoff section
why_it_works: ground flip signals a change from problem to people

style: aerial map stage, pinned props, glow type

finding: One symmetric room shot (prison corridor, vanishing-point centred) is reused as the base plate for six beats: figures in white uniforms (cut-outs 10% frame height, in rows) are added, multiplied, swapped to guard uniforms, or placed behind bars; the camera stays centred so the plate acts as a stage
why_it_works: one environment plus changing populations shows change without cutting away; symmetry gives order
use_when: a story of groups changing in one place

finding: Yellow marker label for names ('Philip Zimbardo', arrow pointing at the tiny man on the lawn) and for one key word per line ('2 a.m.' in yellow italic inside a serif line); a yellow cloth bag recoloured over a prisoner's head is the only colour in the shot
why_it_works: one yellow used for label, number and hood links the three

finding: Figures pop into the corridor in rows (3, then 12, then 24) as the line says the count grows; guards appear in grey uniforms in a separate row in front of the prisoners; scale of every figure in the row is the same so depth reads by position only
why_it_works: counting-by-adding repeats a cut-out; uniform scale keeps the stage legible

finding: 25 soft transitions: slow fade between corridor stage and grainy archive stills; a venetian-blind horizontal-line wipe for 'after six days'; blur-in from a face close-up to the next
why_it_works: line wipe is a prison-bar/blind metaphor in the transition
use_when: time jump in a themed film

finding: ASL 1.0, 9.8 events per 10 s, max 5 s on the corridor stage; the peak speed of camera is at the very start of the shot (median peak 0.0) i.e. a snap-in then settle
why_it_works: snap-in then hold matches voice phrasing

finding: Fully CG 16:9 short in teal/orange: a delivery rider at night, close-ups of a face lit by the phone and laptop (teal light on one side, orange on the other), laptop UI pop-up, drones with bags in glowing outlines; the grade is a strict two-colour split (teal shadows, amber highlights)
why_it_works: complementary split gives depth and mood with no extra graphics

finding: Camera moves are slow push-in on faces and a locked-off over-the-shoulder laptop shot; 11 drifts and 6 holds, zoom up to 1.74, peak around 0.45; wide aerial of the roofs to open and a rooftop wide to close
why_it_works: cinematic grammar: wide, close, over-shoulder, wide

finding: Subtitles are monospace white/teal, left-aligned beside the character ('OH MAN, I'M GETTING LATE...'), sound words in caps; a terminal '#' card on black at the end
why_it_works: mono subtitle fits the tech theme and separates in-world speech from narration

finding: ASL 1.25, 7.7 per 10 s; each action beat (rider puts the bag, checks the phone, opens the laptop) gets 2-3 shots from different angles within 2.5 s
why_it_works: coverage of a simple action in 3 angles reads as film

finding: 3D-ish Victorian scene: an elevator platform with a cut-out man in a top hat on a wooden cage, ropes, a crowd along the bottom and a glass hall behind; the whole is warm orange and brown wood against pale blue-grey; each pose is a separate render (man, assistant, crowd) so the scene can be re-framed
why_it_works: one hue family plus one cool background keeps a complex scene readable

finding: Caption on a solid teal rectangle (white serif, tight padding) set where the eye is, with the key phrase slightly larger, and on white cards the text is large (about 6%) with a faint skyscraper silhouette watermark at the bottom-left
why_it_works: coloured block label guarantees legibility on busy wood, and the teal is the complement of the orange scene

finding: A building facade is built storey by storey: red-brick low building, then taller stacked blocks (6 floors), one floor highlights in yellow as the line says a number, then it jumps to a skyline of towers; each storey is one stepped pop of 0.1-0.2 s
why_it_works: height is shown by adding floors in time

finding: A rope hangs down the frame centre and the camera tilts down along it to reveal the cage, then down further to the dead bodies at the base; vertical tilt with ease-out, 3 s long, text appears word by word at the side of the rope
why_it_works: vertical motion fits the vertical subject

finding: 104 events in 69 s (ASL 0.66, 15 per 10 s); 53 holds and 40 stepped; white text cards for dates ('1854') and the hold at the climax of a drop from the platform
why_it_works: stepped movement keeps the render looking hand-animated

finding: Detective-board opening: grey archive photos with yellow connecting lines, a newspaper clipping 'SECRET MEETING' stuck at the corner, a house photo with a yellow rectangle outline, lines running between portraits at different tilts
why_it_works: lines between photos explain who links to whom without words

finding: Colour used as a block: a full-frame mustard-yellow page with a photo torn into the top, a 'CLASSIFIED' red rubber stamp over a silhouette of a table, a heavy wood door; palette inside is greyscale + yellow + red stamp
why_it_works: stamp and yellow page add document texture while the chapter break is a loud single colour

finding: World map in light grey with a dotted-grain texture, a yellow dot marking a city, and a fire explosion cut-out dropped on a region; two halves of the map drift apart as 'are drifting apart' is shown by a split
why_it_works: movement of the map halves performs the verb

finding: Yellow tape/marker underlines on single words in B&W room photos ('Labour:' plaque, 'Western world', hotel name 'De Bilderberg'), and names set small beside the head; pale paper cards with a ghost headline watermark ('SECRET MEETINGS TO SHAPE THE WORLD') behind black text
why_it_works: watermark of the headline adds a layer to a blank card
use_when: text-only card in a topic with a catchphrase

finding: Pans (45) and pull-outs (20) on stepped footage (42 of 69 shots); portraits are pulled out from a face to reveal the table, ending on the whole room; zoom range 0.49-2.0
why_it_works: face-to-room pull-out gives context after identity

style: B&W archive, yellow lines and tape

finding: 43s piece of 50 shots, ASL 0.87s, median 0.8s; many events are 0.13-0.23s (shots 2-5 together last 0.7s) used as stutter beats, followed by a 1.3s resolved shot. Long/short alternation, not constant rate
why_it_works: burst of micro-events reads as a single beat; the resolved shot afterwards lets the line be read
use_when: a phrase lands word by word and each word needs its own tick

finding: Each scene is a different 'poster world' (black type slate, pink polaroid grid, white purple-cow slide, mint isometric bars, grey product sheet, cinematic silhouette) joined by one constant chrome layer: Kodak Portra 400 film-frame text and corner ticks on 9:16 frames, tiny mono caps top/bottom
why_it_works: the recurring micro-type frame ties unrelated art directions together so the collage reads as one film
use_when: scenes change style but the piece must still feel authored as one

finding: Photo collage scene: four portraits as square cards with green and pink block stickers, a pencil and an eraser lying across the corner, hand-written 'every' above; cards sit on grid paper with registration ticks. Pencil/eraser are the only cutouts that break the grid
why_it_works: stationery props sell the physical desk without any drop shadow noise
use_when: a list of people/examples needs to feel tabletop, not UI

finding: Emphasis word gets a solid green highlight block behind it (first frame 'Rule' in a green box) or a different colour and bigger weight ('WIN' in green on a stack 'That's / how you / WIN' with size ladder small-medium-huge); rest stays white or black Helvetica-like
why_it_works: one accent hue per piece marks only the word the voice stresses; size ladder gives the hierarchy
use_when: the key word of the line must pop on a clean slide

finding: Type slam: huge white letters ('Do that', rotated 'Do') blur-smear out from the frame edge over black, motion-blurred along the movement axis, then a hard cut to a white page with a black block labelled THE MARKET; 4 frames around the cut show heavy blur still present at -2..+1
why_it_works: blur as speed cue stands in for a wipe; the white/black swap resets the screen
use_when: a punchline lands and the next scene must start on a clean ground

finding: Camera mix across 50 shots: drift 20, hold 13, pan 9, pull-out 8, push-in 6, rotate 6; pull-outs outnumber push-ins and zoom stays 0.8-1.0 (a 1.3s pull-out to 0.95, then 0.805 stepped). Mostly small moves, big motion is reserved
why_it_works: restraint makes the few big moves read as events
use_when: planning a camera plan: default drift/hold, spend big moves on the key line

finding: Full-bleed gradient grounds (mint green, deep red glow, teal night, orange) with film grain and light-leak dust, carrying one outlined UI widget; grounds are saturated and near-flat so type has a quiet field
why_it_works: flat saturated ground with grain keeps type legible and feels filmic rather than flat vector
use_when: scenes with little imagery need depth

style: poster-world kinetic type, Kodak frame chrome

finding: Scene grammar alternates dense 'world' scenes (green felt wall with pinned paper, pinned polaroid on grid mat, grey grid paper with black dimples) with near-empty white or black type slates carrying one phrase. Dense scene always has a single type line low in the frame over a darkened band, never over the busy area
why_it_works: empty slate after a dense scene rests the eye; text sits where the image is quiet
use_when: voice line follows a visually heavy beat

finding: Fake-UI entrances: iMessage bubbles type in, grey bubble then blue bubble with highlight on the key words 'pitching' and 'trust'; green pill button with a cursor taps 'Features'; search field types text. UI chrome replaces animation of drawn objects
why_it_works: familiar interface shapes carry meaning (sell vs trust) with zero explanation
use_when: a contrast between two behaviours (pitching vs helping) needs a visual

finding: Directional motion blur on the text as an entrance: 'But you still' appears vertically stretched/smeared with logo icons blurred around it, resolving in 2-3 frames. Also words stacked repeated ('I'm sorry' large, small, cropped by the frame edge) over emoji stickers
why_it_works: smear reads as speed so text needs no easing curve to feel kinetic
use_when: a word enters from outside the frame

finding: Face-grid mosaic: many small B&W portrait tiles with white outline frames and one face dissolved into noise/static; the sentence sits across the tiles in white, kerned tightly. Pixel-dissolve stands in for 'they don't trust'
why_it_works: identical-format tiles = a crowd; the one corrupted tile is the point
use_when: showing a crowd where one element is the subject

finding: Light-flare transition: a fluorescent tube in a film still blooms over 2 frames to full white-yellow wash, then next frame returns text over the still; also a plain white flash frame between scenes (frame 3-4 of the sheet)
why_it_works: bright flash hides the swap and is physically motivated by the lamp in the picture
use_when: cutting from a live-action still to a graphic

finding: Palette locked to near-black green felt + one lime green accent, with exceptions of orange book cover and purple club still; the book cover cutout is the only saturated orange object and gets the largest headline after it ('THATS THE WHOLE SECRET' in red on newsprint)
why_it_works: accent colour is reserved for interactive/key things
use_when: building a brand palette for the film

style: dark felt desk plus fake UI

finding: Every scene is a metaphor object built on graph/blueprint paper: glossy jelly shapes (red, yellow, green) with a tiny stick figure climbing them; green chat bubbles as stepping platforms; brain cutouts on blue blueprint with white-outlined stickers; Windows XP desktop with dialog boxes. Grid ground is constant, objects change
why_it_works: one ground texture = continuity; a 20px human figure gives scale and story to any abstract shape
use_when: abstract idea (effort, thinking) needs a character without full animation

finding: Brain cutouts with thick white sticker outline and halftone-grain shading, in multiples, with a red double-exclamation sticker; the neon green stroked 'THINK' wordmark with black outline sits across the centre. Outline width about 6-8px at 1080 wide, same on every cutout
why_it_works: uniform white die-cut edge unifies photos of different origin and lifts them off a saturated blue
use_when: photo cutouts sit on saturated ground

finding: Phone lock screen scene: phone rises into frame over the blue background, then notification cards stack in one after another with app icons (WhatsApp, Instagram); an XP window slides over from the right to end the beat. Elements arrive staggered ~0.2s apart
why_it_works: familiar notification stack reads at a glance
use_when: a list of messages / reasons is needed

finding: Live-action cut: football shot with giant white 'Nike' word in the frame, the word slides behind the player (depth: text between layers) as the camera follows; the following scene is a cutout athlete sticker on a grid with chat bubbles, so the brand-photo to collage handoff happens with text staying put
why_it_works: text sandwiched between foreground subject and background reads as filmed, not overlaid
use_when: video footage plus title must feel like one shot

finding: Chat bubble held in extreme close-up and drifting up the frame ('so you start'), fades to a rear layer as the next scene wipes in; a vertical film-edge strip with the word CAMPAIGN rotates in sideways at left of a phone mockup with a blurred word 'Makes' resolving over 2 frames
why_it_works: vertical strip adds a second reading direction and masks the cut
use_when: a side title/spine is needed in 9:16

finding: Dense type-only moments alternate with objects: white slate with two-line statement 'you're finishing it in your head' (centered, black, 2 weights); condensed all-caps display words (EMOTION, STORY, EDITORS) in red with white offset stroke, repeated as a ghost row behind; word 'ACCESS' green over Ae file icon
why_it_works: two type voices: calm Helvetica for sentences, loud condensed for the single noun
use_when: a sentence has one noun that is the subject

finding: CTA: green 3D folder with Ae app icon tilted and floating, comment word in quotes below; a black bar and screenshot of a post flank the white slate, borders crop the picture (letterbox black above and below at 4:5 inside 9:16)
why_it_works: glossy 3D objects against flat paper give depth without shadow engine

finding: Opens on a tweet-composer mock: cursor types the quoted name letter by letter (a character per frame in the 4 cut frames), a video card with play icon sits under it. Typed text is the entrance; no motion of the card
why_it_works: typing is a built-in reveal that matches speech rate and needs no easing
use_when: a quote or name introduces the topic

finding: Giant yellow condensed display letters with black extrusion ('WITHOUT GIVING UP ALCOHOL') split into stacked lines of different size, the last word wrapped around a 3D bottle cutout (letters pass behind the bottle, 'ALCOHO' rises letter by letter over 4 frames) on a Windows XP green-hill wallpaper
why_it_works: type interleaved with the object (in front of and behind it) makes depth with no 3D
use_when: a noun in the line has a prop

finding: Coins drift across white while 'SELL IT TO' types in; then the words jump to a huge extruded 'THEM IT' sliding off the top while a coin leads 'COST YOU' across the frame (text trails the coin as if pushed). Coins are pixel-art with black offset shadow and halftone
why_it_works: three sizes of coin give parallax depth; text tracks a coin for a sense of one physical thing
use_when: money/value metaphor with a single moving object

finding: Variation between clean poster (grey grid paper, barcode, ALREADY / SUFFERING FROM in tall condensed type centered, vignette darkening corners) and a tight film still with a circular iris crop. Posters keep 20%+ of the frame empty above and below the type block
why_it_works: vignette plus empty margins make the type block feel printed on a physical poster

finding: Text placed between layers over live action: 'Make it' above the figure and 'IMPOSSIBLE' across his body, with the letters 'PO' knocked to outline so the subject shows through; later a face tight crop with 'to ignore' printed into the forehead
why_it_works: selective knock-out keeps the subject readable while the word stays huge
use_when: big word over a person footage

finding: Median shot 0.33s, ASL 0.85, 11.5 events/10s; 7 stepped (posterized 12fps) shots. The word-per-event type builds ('THAT'S NOT MOTIVATION' / 'THAT'S POSITIONING' / 'THAT'S HELPING') swap in place in 3-4 steps with ghost duplicates behind
why_it_works: in-place swap with ghost trail keeps the layout stable while the word changes
use_when: repetitive parallel statement (not X, but Y)

style: tweet UI, extruded type, XP wallpaper

finding: Site-promo, not a collage explainer: monitor and phone mockups lit by window-blind stripes on wood; a rotating 3D carousel of vertical cards on a black glossy floor with green rim light and reflections. Camera orbits and pushes toward one card ('what's even better?' fills the frame at 7s)
why_it_works: carousel with reflection floor presents many items in one continuous move and ends by pushing into one
use_when: showing a set of screens/items then focusing on one

finding: Hand-written script words ('Editors', 'Site', 'After effects') in white chalk-like script mixed with clean sans ('i barely see') overlaid on the mockup, lines overlapping the device; script word placed on the floor reflection area below the screen
why_it_works: script plus sans = human voice over a product shot

finding: Ends on a mock comment sheet: iOS keyboard slides up and the text 'comment link' is typed; hard cut from the green carousel to a flat white UI. Dark-green-to-white swap, no transition
why_it_works: UI of the platform in which the CTA happens
use_when: call to action that happens in a known app

finding: Scene opens on a full-bleed underwater photo with surface light rays; tiny type ('Marketing') in the centre, then the prop (bottle, diamond) floats down through the same frame, turning into 'VALUES' lettering. Photo stays, objects and words change
why_it_works: one environment as ground; words become part of the scene

finding: Cutout globe with a face and red curved lettering 'LOUD WORLD' around it on black space; an astronaut cutout plants a flag with the brand mark on a moon surface and casts a flat shadow; later the astronaut is next to a yellow block 'YOU'. 3D toy photos with a hard cast shadow on a plain floor
why_it_works: consistent hard shadow direction glues cutouts to a floor; text curved on object follows its form

finding: Number and letter bubbles (iMessage typing dots, keypad keys '2 ABC', '7') bounce into the white frame and fly out; bubble words 'have to be', 'thing', 'about' appear in sequence with the keypad digits tumbling around them
why_it_works: falling particles give a visible, silent beat between words
use_when: white slate with a phrase typed in several beats

finding: Screen-recording style switch: a poster viewed in a Mac window, then macOS wallpaper with a notification banner; the next beat is a pure white slate with 'That's it.' in a typewriter font, shifted in from the left by a wipe. Interface scale jumps from desktop to a full-bleed page
why_it_works: zooming out of UI to full page is a match-cut in scale
use_when: going from a detail (notification) to a statement

finding: WhatsApp conversation as the narrator ('Why?', 'Because Nike never talks.'): bubbles appear one at a time on beige ground, the answer in green; then a live-action football clip with a one-line caption replacing the bubble thread
why_it_works: Q and A bubble pairs let a two-voice argument sit on one frame

finding: Lime green slate (#9be564-like) with dark condensed lines 'THAT'S WHAT THEY STAND FOR' building by sliding over each other; then Jordan photo cutouts on white with a green panel growing from the right carrying running text. Green full-bleed is used for the single message, white for the rest
why_it_works: one loud ground reserved for the thesis line
use_when: marking the thesis moment of a piece

style: UI bubbles, cutout toys, lime slate

finding: Cuts to low-resolution football clips: tight crop of a boot is upscaled to a soft blur of pink/orange blocks across 4 frames (cut frames show no detail), and a 16:9 clip is letterboxed small inside black 9:16 with a caption on top. The better scenes hide low-res by blur plus text; the clip inside a black frame with margins reads as cheap
why_it_works: low-res footage passes only when covered by type or used for one beat
use_when: stock/archive footage of low resolution is the only option

finding: Sticker burst: spiky star shapes in red, teal and green sit between words of the headline, angry sun-emoji cutouts with white outline pop behind 'BUSINESS'; an Iron Man poster cutout crops the sides. Everything has a white die-cut edge and sits on white
why_it_works: stars and emoji act as punctuation between words and fill the white without clutter
use_when: a loud hook on a white ground

finding: Chat UI is the stage: an iMessage thread types out line by line ('If you can't...'), the keyboard rises with autocorrect suggestions, text field in dark mode; a single blue bubble 'YOU!' with 'Read 11:40PM' receipt sits centered on white. Messages use real UI timing, one line every 0.8-1s
why_it_works: a familiar thread tells a person's pain without any footage

finding: Windows XP wallpaper with a draggable window holding a B&W portrait; yellow cursor-hand and small yellow tag labels ('build anything') point at pieces; folder icons on the right. Hand cursor clicks and drags, tags at 8-10% of frame width
why_it_works: cursor as a pointer inside the scene directs the eye without arrows
use_when: showing a fix being applied to something

finding: White grid slate with typed line 'The Solution is Simple|' where the cursor blinks, then 'Build' with the word 'system' inside a lime highlight pill sliding in; then a hiring-card UI with avatars and Hire/Reject buttons with a lime marker stroke over the key phrase. Lime marker highlight = emphasis device throughout
why_it_works: highlighter on the line is the cheapest hierarchy

finding: Closing: top-down desk shot (hands on keyboard, coffee mug, phone) in dark wood with soft vignette, words overlaid in dim white and orange ('without you'); camera pushes slowly in, then cut to a black field with glowing teal Ae icons and a framed UI mock with a thin green keyline
why_it_works: live-action top-down is the only 'real' moment, giving the piece an emotional dip before the CTA
use_when: contrast between collage and filmed beat

style: chat UI, XP desktop, lime marker

finding: Light, airy 3D-render look: white ground with soft pastel gradient floor (lavender to mint) and a lime wave line; clay-like 3D props (blue statue, wall clock with serif 'time' in a red highlight, Ae file icon as glossy slab) with soft shadows. Type is thin geometric sans plus an italic serif accent word
why_it_works: soft gradient floor and glossy slabs give depth with no heavy shadow; serif italic word contrasts with sans
use_when: clean product/finance register, not gritty collage

finding: Number counter on a statue (9 to 202 to 21) with small label under, then big word 'starting' in thin sans lower on the frame; shot 'deadlines are tight' appears with the sun-and-window light pattern on a pink wall. Word and object enter blurred then sharp
why_it_works: a numeric tick is an easy beat in time with speech

finding: Ae file icon slab tumbles across the website mock, rotating in 3D from corner to corner and leaving frame at the bottom, while a text 'earnedits.com provides you real open AEP project files' stays fixed; the slab is the only moving element (sheet frames 9-14 show rotation about the long axis)
why_it_works: one moving 3D object over a static screenshot adds life without disturbing readability

finding: Numbered pill list '01 Take proven ideas / 02 Re-edit them / 03 Finish your projects faster' stacks as grey rounded buttons with shadow, each added every ~0.5s, the earlier ones shifting up. Final CTA 'Comment LINK' in small type on a pale floor with the green wave line
why_it_works: numbers on stacked chips give order and rhythm for a three-step promise

finding: Open on stacked UI sheets (app store listing, notifications) with 'BE HONEST' in a purple highlighted display type, then swap to a hot orange ground with the cartoon cutout and 'are you Really obsessed' in white heavy sans; transition is a push where the orange panel slides over the UI in 2-3 frames. Orange is used only for this hook
why_it_works: loud ground and sharp panel push mark the hook as different from the body

finding: Brand logos on neutral grounds as the evidence: Amazon smile icon on a frosted grid of app tiles with floating pale-blue word tags ('over', 'convenience'), Uber logo on white then a map screen with a moving car and a notification card, Netflix logo in red on black with a 'removed' red stamp. Each brand gets its own colour world, logo centered, tags small
why_it_works: logo is the hero and the tag words are subtext at 1/6 scale
use_when: case-study scenes that mention brand names

finding: Scrabble-like letter tiles tumble in 3D on green felt and spell 'solution' (letters rotate, drop, settle); later 'Solution' is circled in a red hand-drawn ellipse over a green grid mat with a calculator and 'BUILT THEY'RE' in condensed type under window-blind shadow stripes
why_it_works: hand-drawn ellipse marks the one word on a clean surface
use_when: circle the key term in a collage layer

finding: Diagonal window-blind shadow stripes laid over green grid paper, a tilted calculator cutout and sticky notes; shadow bands cross everything at about 25deg and make the flat mat read as a desk in sunlight. Same device in DRzcFdBjDPG and DT-tehKDNRH (wood table)
why_it_works: one cheap shadow overlay unifies flat layers
use_when: collage of flat pieces needs one light source

finding: Filmed figure at a desk at night lit by screens with text 'Solve the right problem deeply' then 'Growth follows naturally' in white sans at lower third; static shot, text swaps, then cut to the black closing scene with glowing teal Ae icons and one framed UI with a thin green keyline (same ending as DTaQHn1DEll)
why_it_works: a still filmed hold lets the final line breathe before the CTA
use_when: the closing thought of the piece

finding: Phone-camera viewfinder as the camera: the frame has iOS camera UI (shutter, mode strip PHOTO/VIDEO) and 'photographs' a desk with a diagonal window-light shadow; the 'subject' (a contract, a visa stamp) slides in under the lens and the picture pushes in 1.0 to ~1.3 with focus pulling soft to sharp. Text sits on the object, not on the UI
why_it_works: a camera UI justifies zooms/focus pulls and frames each object like a shot
use_when: inspecting documents or objects in sequence

finding: Old-OS notepad ('Memo') window whose text reflows as words are typed: 'People don't just buy PRODUCTS!!' in large typewriter type at a 3-line stack; a phone cutout slides across and eclipses part of the line. Heading emphasised by caps in heavier weight, not colour
why_it_works: typed UI text is a reveal; occlusion adds depth
use_when: a rule stated in a document

finding: Data-UI scene: ranking list rows with avatars and green score chips; a radial progress ring counts 66 to 80%; a mind-map node 'Referrals' grows a green pill then a red pill 'Recommendations' branching with thin lines. Counting number and pills grow in 0.3-0.5s
why_it_works: mini infographics with one number moving give proof without a chart

finding: Top-down desk scenes: green cutting mat with white grid, vintage cassette, laptop at the top, wooden floor, big diagonal shadow band across, coloured chat bubbles in orange/green floating over; later retro handheld, iPod, cards and pencils scattered at random angles on grid. Props at 5-15 deg rotations, few overlaps
why_it_works: scatter at varied angles reads as a real flat-lay; shadow band adds time of day
