finding: Search-bar finale: Google-like pill types the query letter by letter, results page rises into place with the brand listing; the whole page is zoomed so the result row fills the frame by the end (push-in ~1.6x). Ends flat, no outro motion
why_it_works: typed search is a universal CTA grammar, push-in focuses the answer

finding: Phone-camera and Instagram UI as the world: a hand holds a phone over the desk, the screen shows an editing grid with words 'YOUR BRAND IS NOT' placed as tiles; the shot dollies into the screen until the screen fills the frame and becomes the next scene (scale-match cut)
why_it_works: zoom into a screen is a continuous transition into UI content
use_when: moving from a real-world object into a screen

finding: Colour-code anatomy: hex label '#B5179E' in red sans, a struck-through 'not your colors' with a crossed O and a script word 'Colors' in teal, a green swatch bar of 3 squares; strike-through and cross applied by hand-drawn red marks. Three type voices (grotesque, script, mono hex) on a white page
why_it_works: each voice maps to one role (rule, flourish, data)
use_when: a list of things 'not X' being negated

finding: Edge-to-edge UI mocks used as full backgrounds: iOS Safari share sheet, Facebook composer on an old iPhone with a blue title bar, Instagram profile, Notes app text selection with blue highlight and the iOS selection popover on the words; the text being typed is the headline and the cursor selection is the emphasis
why_it_works: the UI supplies text styling, so no design layer to maintain
use_when: low-budget scenes with a message-first beat

finding: Emoji-sticker collage on grid paper: sunglasses emoji with white die-cut outline at two scales, a circular ring of tiny text around the centre, headline 'Every Happy Customer' overshooting the frame width and cropped; film still of friends at a bowling alley with caption lower-left
why_it_works: oversize cropped headline shows scale; emoji works as a small colour accent

finding: Script word 'story' in thin red cursive handwritten stroke-by-stroke on a pale grid; a camera-flash glare in the corner washes out frame 3 and the title resolves after; portrait photos get a single big word over the chin ('people move forward', 'Consistency' over a tele shot). Flash = punctuation
why_it_works: glare covers the swap and the brush-on script feels human
use_when: emotional word in a business piece

finding: Black ending reuses an identical CTA template as DTaQHn1DEll / DTxZksEDMiQ / DUGJjUEjO_I: glowing Ae icons, then framed UI with green keyline. Reuse reads as a brand sign-off, but the body of the sheet shows many dim, small text lines on black that are unreadable at phone size (about 1% frame height)
why_it_works: template ending is fine; unreadably small subtext is what the better pieces avoid
use_when: design the sign-off, keep microtext as texture only

style: phone UI worlds, hand script accents

finding: Talking-head interleave: a presenter A-roll (cap, white tee, studio bokeh, same framing in 6 separate runs) alternates with 1-3s graphic inserts that are the same collage pieces as in the English pieces (coins, clock, Iron Man poster, search bar, project grid). A-roll stays at about 3-4s runs with only hand gesture motion; inserts carry the cuts
why_it_works: face gives trust, inserts give proof; returns to the same framing so the presenter feels continuous
use_when: film with an on-camera speaker plus explainer graphics

finding: Open: a tweet frame with the presenter's video embedded (play icon), type 'You Must' typed in; then a cutout Iron Man with the presenter's face composited on top of him and yellow tape bands with right-to-left Arabic labels. Poster crop is tight, figure fills ~80% height
why_it_works: famous body plus own face = instant meme-cover hook

finding: Dark-green UI scene with glowing green rim: a fan of vertical screens/cards (ocean, hot orange card, white card) flips through in a row (carousel) and one card flashes yellow-white before cutting to a white slate with the wall clock; each card seen about 0.15s
why_it_works: a quick fan shows variety (many examples) without any card being read
use_when: proof that there are many of something

finding: Arabic type works in the same system: heavy black Arabic on white with a red highlight band behind 'time'-word, coins falling and a '$ 4' price in huge black; words wipe in as horizontal strips ('PROJECT' word split across two lines). RTL does not change position grammar (highlight, extruded black, coin accent)
why_it_works: layout rules survive a script change if weight and contrast are kept

finding: Rotating ring: project thumbnails arranged in a wheel that spins past with 'projects' lettering in front (the wheel rotates about 45deg in 0.5s while text holds still); then the presenter types in a search bar over his own A-roll, and the closing UI frame
why_it_works: static type over a rotating carousel gives parallax between layers

finding: Highlight-and-cursor intro on white: text 'If you use After Effects' types, 'After Effects' gets a lilac selection box with blue handle ticks, small mock UI cards and thumbnails scatter in at random angles around it (about 8 pieces, 2-3 frames apart), screen then cuts to black with a search pill
why_it_works: selection box is a free highlight that matches the topic; scattered thumbnails build 'a lot of stuff' fast
use_when: intro naming a tool or noun

finding: Website mock flies in perspective: a dark site screenshot tilts and zooms from a high angle, blur streaks of text ('Vir' large, warped) appear as it passes; italic serif 'earnedits.com' is the same width as the screenshot. Perspective tilt 20-30deg and ease-out
why_it_works: 3D tilt plus warped giant word = speed on a flat screenshot
use_when: revealing a site or product page

finding: Phone mock (iPhone with green screen) slowly rotates and fills frame; then white page where thumbnails scatter in a loose grid with small arrow glyphs and barcodes between, text 'Real projects' in serif italic overlay; same piece collage recurs as a final recap where all thumbnails return at once (sheet frames 49-52)
why_it_works: recap of all assets in one frame makes the ending a catalogue
use_when: final summary frame of a piece

finding: CTA word 'Link' set in a large high-contrast italic serif over small sans 'comment', centred on white; serif italic is reserved for the one word that is the action. Median shot 0.27s with 9 stepped shots - fastest cut cluster in the batch
why_it_works: serif italic is the only serif in the piece so the eye lands on it

finding: One unifying 3D character: a black glossy thinker statue seated at a laptop in a dark green-lit room, recurring as the background for hook, middle and CTA. Type sits to the left/over the statue's torso in white sans with one italic word ('ideas'). Green rim light on the statue's edges
why_it_works: returning to the same plate bookends the piece and gives the eye a home between UI inserts
use_when: a short piece needs a base location

finding: Camera moves around the statue in the render: orbit and push from over-shoulder to the face, then pull back to the laptop; 'Stop wasting hours' appears as embossed text printed on the dark wall and gets overtaken by the statue as it moves (text sandwiched between wall and subject)
why_it_works: moving through a 3D set gives parallax that flat collage lacks
use_when: opening hook with a hero object

finding: Dolly into laptop: the screen of the laptop grows to fill the frame and becomes the website UI (EarnEdits.com) in a continuous push; later, UI panel zooms and the Ae icons orbit it. Screen-in-scene match cut, ~0.5s
why_it_works: entering the screen is a match cut that explains the product
use_when: moving from setup to product demo

finding: Dense UI mock panels slide up in stacks (poster thumbnails, AE timeline bars, phone with green dial), each panel framed by a hairline; text overlay 'Less searching / Less stress' appears in layers over the stack, the stack blurs behind. Poster thumbs appear as 3-4 columns of vertical cards
why_it_works: dense panels read as 'a lot' while the overlay carries the message

finding: Final line 'Just re-edit proven ideas' built word by word over the statue with a mix of regular sans and one italic emphasised word; then 'Comment LINK and I'll send it' at the same position, 3 frames later. Text position fixed so only words change
why_it_works: fixed text box lets the CTA replace the claim without moving the picture

finding: Object-per-word: handwritten 'selling' over dollars on wood, 'Storytelling' over a clapperboard in a dark vignette, a phone mock with notification stack, a film still of robot toy faces with a hand-lettered word; each key noun gets its own physical prop
why_it_works: objects as nouns let one word per second read without a sentence
use_when: explaining a pair of contrasted nouns (selling vs storytelling)

finding: Black grounds with a single spotlight object: white chess king with chrome pawns scattered with soft shadows; clapperboard in a white circle on black with pill labels 'meaning' and 'emotion' with emoji icons; vignette hard. Contrast 1 bright object : dark field
why_it_works: a lone lit object on black is the strongest emphasis device

finding: A ring of avatar icons rotates around a central person and collapses to one avatar with a green glow; then type wraps on a ring ('selling is about the product') that rotates around a 'Product' disc. Rotating type ring makes a headline into an object
why_it_works: circular layout gives a long phrase a compact footprint
use_when: a sentence that should become an emblem

finding: Word that is the subject is rendered as a hand-scribbled script ('selling' in black marker scribble) in the middle of a clean sans sentence 'so don't just focus on'; the scribble draws in 4 frames. Next, a hand-with-camera cutout sticker stays beside 'tell stories worth caring about'
why_it_works: marker word breaks the sans line and marks the topic word
use_when: naming the wrong thing the viewer should drop

finding: Hard scale from the white slate to a dark site hero ('just for editors') where the headline slides vertically out and in (letters cut at the edge); CTA keyboard and comment sheet follow in white. Light to dark swap is the sign that the piece moves from idea to offer
why_it_works: palette flip marks the structure change

style: single hero props on black, marker script

finding: Near-monochrome grade: black and greyscale renders (chrome Ae icon, B&W presenter) with one lime-green UI accent (pill buttons, progress dots, 'comment LINK' green dot). Grey metallic Ae file cards with a cursor hand clicking them; most frames have under 5% of the area in colour
why_it_works: restricting the accent to interactive UI makes the click target obvious

finding: Light-glow type on chrome: 'Here's a fact' lettering rendered as a glowing outline on dark stone texture with embossing; then 'No one tells you' as bright white with outer glow and a ghost reflection beneath. Cuts every 0.4s in the first 8s. Letterforms blur-resolve in 2 frames
why_it_works: glow gives contrast on a textured dark ground
use_when: title on a dark textured plate

finding: After Effects UI as a stage: an empty timeline screen, 'don't start from an empty timeline' enters word by word (3 words, 3 frames apart, each blurred then sharp) over the timeline panel; then a cursor hand drops AEP file cards into the new-composition dialog, the cards stack at slight fan angles
why_it_works: the tool's own empty state is the problem picture
use_when: showing a pain moment inside the software

finding: Mosaic wall: 5 x 4 grid of earlier clip thumbnails, each tile edge to edge, the camera pushes through and the grid is the previous pieces; later an app-store-like card strip scrolls horizontally with paging dots at the bottom (10 dots) and a green button. Grid evidence of volume
why_it_works: mosaic of 20 tiles delivers 'many examples' in one still

finding: Calm ending: rolling counters on a stats panel ('viral' with numbers ticking), 'Subscribe now on EarnEdits.com' in white with the site mock slowly rising, then a B&W presenter held 3s with the CTA words 'start editing like a pro today' appearing word by word then 'comment LINK' in large type. Slower than the first half (ASL 1.2 overall, tail shots ~1s)
why_it_works: slower tail leaves time to read the instruction

finding: Hand-and-UI motion graphics: a lime 'Let' pill with a red arrow button and an orange circle button sit on black and are tapped (button press with scale 0.9 and shadow), a phone on wood with window-blind shadow shows lock screen text with a speech-bubble sticker 'NAH IT WIN.' that pops. Tap feedback of 2-3 frames is the beat
why_it_works: press feedback is a free micro-motion that marks the beat

finding: Notes-app writing as narration: 'Idea / You woke up to write down' types in a white Notes page, a checklist panel then takes the line 'They can't fake your energy / story / don't have your...' with a blue checklist bullet that fills. Text rows add every ~0.7s, previous rows move up
why_it_works: a checklist structure says 'three things' with no counting graphics

finding: Spark burst on white: green four-point stars scale up from the text 'But brands can't' in 2-3 sizes, leaving small dots; then a replicate wall: the word 'replicate' repeated as a faded text wallpaper with one line in sharp black and the key word in green (large). Wall repeats 8 lines at descending opacity
why_it_works: repeated faded copies make a field of text, one sharp line is the focal

finding: Stage-prop plates: a clapperboard and a camera hang from a cable on dark teal while 'INNOVATING' and 'THEM' in huge white condensed type slam across and a yellow 'WATCH' tag follows; the props stay in the corner and sway. A fire still with hard 'FIRE' lettering in cyan 3D bevel overlays
why_it_works: a swaying prop gives the static type slab a little life
use_when: a big word sequence over an almost empty frame

finding: Ends inside the iOS camera UI: clapperboard filling the viewfinder with the caption 'After effect users' on a red tape label, shutter button at the bottom; the board is filmed, then pushes in until 'Visit now / download it' appears; mode strip (SLO-MO / VIDEO / PHOTO) is the scene's chrome (same device as DU-zVUXCD-r)
why_it_works: viewfinder UI is a frame that justifies the push and the click

finding: Story-with-evidence structure: year '1959' in red type over a sky-and-cloud photo, a STOP sign sliding in and the car (VW Beetle photo cutout, B&W) driving along a road strip at the bottom; red label bar 'Volkswagen sold a small ugly car' across the car. Picture fills the top 60%, road 15%, label band at lower third
why_it_works: year plus object plus one label bar = a complete case-study card in 2 seconds

finding: Archive-print cutouts: B&W newspaper-style photos (Beetle, 1940s car, auction scene, George Washington dollar-bill portrait, Harvard crest with red and green) each with a red tape label carrying the claim; label is the same slab shape (red box, white condensed caps, dark outline) every time. Rival-car ad is placed on denim-blue stitched background in a framed inset
why_it_works: one reusable label shape lets 8 different photos read as one system
use_when: series of archive photos with claims

finding: Rust-orange tiled ground with a face cutout under a white bar and 'DESIGNED BY' red label with eyes drawn on the bar: a contentious figure is reduced to a cropped face with a censor bar and cartoon eyes. The censor bar covers the eyes and the cutout stays small, which avoids a literal image
why_it_works: abstracting a sensitive figure to a bar-and-eyes sticker lowers risk and reads as a joke
use_when: a figure that must not be shown literally

finding: Words enter inside the picture: 'THIS IS THE PRATFALL EFFECT' as bold green condensed words rising from behind the portrait's hands (text masked by the picture's edge, the portrait holds the sign); Harvard 'RESEARCH SHOWS' label on the crest; retro XP monitor with the blue-sky wallpaper carrying 'THAT WHEN A BRAND ADMITS A FLAW' in the screen; 'TRUST' stepping up a staircase line with tiny people at each step 'SKYROCKETS'
why_it_works: text emerging from behind the subject binds text to picture and gives a free reveal wipe
use_when: a headline that rises from an image

finding: Imperfection copy gag: a huge hand holds a browser window with 'IMPERFECTION FEELS FAKE' typed; the words change in place to 'FEELS HUMAN' (3 swaps); pizza flies in from top, shifts to a cardboard disc with 'crust tasted like cardboard' handwritten beneath. Text swap in place on the same frame with a red-white box flicker
why_it_works: in-place text correction demonstrates 'admit the flaw'

finding: Product-page scene: jacket photo on a pale page with 'DON'T BUY THIS JACKET' in black condensed caps, a red 'THE RESULTS ARE THE SAME' bar stamped on the jacket; then the planet-with-face emoji spinning inside a circular text ring; camera settles with slow push-ins (about 1.05x) on each held page
why_it_works: slow push over a held page keeps a still alive

finding: Hook: yellow ground with white sunburst rays, a shocked person cutout with a brain popping above his head (3D brain with a white die-cut edge), red condensed 'MARKETERS found it' sandwiching the brain; type is in front of the body and behind the brain. Rays converge at the brain, so the eye goes to the brain
why_it_works: radial rays point at the subject; layered text puts the brain on top

finding: Tabletop-photo plates: a top-down desk (glasses, coffee, notebook, phone) with paper sheet carrying the text in a stencil-like green outline; a hand holds a magnifier over a cookie-consent dialog, then a calendar countdown; each scene is a photo plate, the dialog and text are composed in, magnifier ring is the only moving prop
why_it_works: photographic desk grounds sell realism; the magnifier acts as a pointer
use_when: inspecting a UI or text closely

finding: Pure type slates on black: 'WHEN IT FEELS VALUABLE' then 'IT FEELS URGENT' in bold white sans, one phrase per slate, second slate typed to full width with the last word cropped by the frame edge; slates hold ~0.7s. Slate cuts contrast with 1.5-2s photo plates
why_it_works: alternate dense photo and empty type slate sets the pace and gives breathing room
use_when: a rule line follows an example

finding: Airplane-window frame: a hand holds a red Airbnb-style card up to the window with clouds and wing; text 'FIVE PEOPLE ARE LOOKING AT THIS' is typed in the sky over the wing. The window oval is a mask that frames the scene so the text follows the oval's curvature
why_it_works: an oval mask is a stronger frame than a rectangle and echoes the scene

finding: Streetwear case: a person in a skeleton hoodie with a neon green then yellow face-mask in a stepped (12fps) colour cycle, 'Supreme' red logo box across his chest; then plain 'Supreme' logo slate on white, black. Face colour swaps in steps at 3-frame intervals, which keeps the loud look with minimal animation
why_it_works: colour cycling of one element gives energy with no movement

finding: Edge: hand-written note paper 'THE PRODUCT ISN'T RARE / THE FEELING IS ENGINEERED' with a red marker ellipse drawn around 'ENGINEERED' (the stroke draws in 6 frames), then black slate 'THEY JUST FIGURED OUT' in gold, 'HOW TO USE YOUR OWN BRAIN', then the CTA mock (phone with site) over sky
why_it_works: marker stroke is a draw-on that doubles as emphasis

style: photo plates, red marker, stepped colour

finding: Colour-per-scene grounds picked for the brand: wood table + paper calendar, terracotta with a grid of black person icons (rows added until 6x5), pale grid with a $ money bag, olive green with Spotify logo, then red slates 'NO REWARD / NO INCENTIVE' in white-on-black label bars. Each scene has exactly one icon or logo at 30-40% of frame
why_it_works: one flat colour and one icon per beat keeps the scene instantly readable

finding: Icon-grid count-up: person icons appear in rows over 4 frames (from 15 to 30 at roughly 2 rows per step), then a small word 'voluntarily' fades in under the grid. Stepped, non-eased; the count reads as 'millions'
why_it_works: the pictogram multiplication is a count without numbers

finding: Phone floats in a cloud-sky ground and tilts into place (rotates from 60deg to upright), screen shows a listening counter with ticking figures; clouds sit as layers in front of and behind the phone so the phone drifts through them. Stepped 12fps feel on the tilt
why_it_works: cloud layers in front and behind give depth for free
use_when: a hero device in an environment

finding: Old-OS window on a green hills wallpaper types the sentence 'The most brilliant zero dollar marketing campaign in history' one character per frame inside a small grey dialog; the window is small (30% of width) and the sentence needs 6 lines of typing time. Big claim sits in a small window
why_it_works: typing time is the beat; a small window means the wallpaper still shows
use_when: a claim that benefits from being read slowly

finding: Mustard ground with a white bar chart whose bars grow stepwise while the sentence 'WRAPPED DOESN'T SELL SPOTIFY' types over it in white condensed, and next scene: B&W photo of a man facing a mirror with serif-less all-caps line; headline blocks use two weights with a coloured underline bar (brown, then red) under 'JUST SHARE IT' / 'DEFEND IT'
why_it_works: underline bar is a swap-in emphasis that costs one rectangle
use_when: the word that replaces another in a repeated phrase

finding: Brand logo scenes with their own ground: Apple Music pink-red, Amazon Music teal to grey, YouTube Music red with play button, each held ~1.2s; social icons (Instagram, X, WhatsApp, Facebook) orbit '400M' and shuffle position between steps; a dollar bill hangs from a string over 'ALMOST NOTHING'. Logos flat, no cut-out edge needed
why_it_works: a ground colour taken from the brand carries identity without a photo

finding: Close-up hand holding a phone with a lock screen in a street, camera locked, the screen text swaps; then a blue slate with 'THE BRAND THAT MAKES' in tiny type left-aligned (huge empty ground, text 6% of height). Ending uses scale contrast: huge empty, tiny line
why_it_works: small text in a big field makes the last line feel quiet and final

finding: Subject cutout in an expanding-ripple ground: a Buffett caricature figure on a card, then red-and-white concentric ripple rings radiate from him while a counter ticks '300' to '381' on a white tag under him; next scene fills the frame with fanned dollar bills, then the Greek flag with olives on a table and a country-map cutout. Number on a tag at the foot of the figure, rings as a bullseye
why_it_works: rings point to the subject and read as value pulsing out
use_when: a big number attached to a person

finding: Word-level kinetic type with weight changes: 'HE'S' / 'BEEN SELLING' in white heavy sans on a blue felt ground with a standing figure; 'BUT HE IS NOT SPENDING IT' in yellow-and-white heavy italic over a portrait, with 'NOT' in yellow; the big numbers ('S&P 500', '80%' in red on a blackboard) are 3x the verb size. Burned-in small caption in the bottom 10% repeats the sentence in thin white
why_it_works: big words are the stressed ones, caption is the full sentence for sound-off viewers
use_when: dual-layer text: emphasis words plus a plain caption

finding: Hands on a green felt desk with money: top-down hands count bills, a hand pushes a stack and a red 'WHY' tag slaps onto the palm; the shot then iris-closes to a circle around the hand (black vignette edges) before 'BECAUSE HE'S DONE THIS BEFORE' prints in white. Hand cutout is a photo (flesh tone) with hard shadows
why_it_works: iris closes attention onto one detail

finding: Flat full-bleed colour slates for years: royal blue slate 'In 1999' / 'And 2007' with each year in a green highlighted box; each slate changes ground (blue, black, green felt, red) per beat, pure colour with a vintage-framed portrait and bills wreath as the only image
why_it_works: colour change alone tells the viewer the topic moved

finding: Numeric counter '20' to '200' to '230 PERCENT' in a red-outlined retro pixel frame, then a US-flag badge slides in and the red slate 'THAT'S VERY HIGH' builds by scale (letters grow word-by-word from 80% to 110% size)
why_it_works: counting up to the number gives the beat; size growth stresses 'very high'

finding: Clipboard question scene: pennies/coins fall from above onto the clipboard and bounce out as 'The real question is' types; then close-up with a pile of cash on his head, 'WAITING' in red caps on black; the end card uses sky ground, retro camera and a phone rising from the bottom with the CTA
why_it_works: physical things falling into the shot are cheap secondary motion

style: felt desk props, loud number slates

finding: Brand-driven world: pastel sky and green hill ground (XP wallpaper register) with an energy drink can floating in, red/blue condensed type behind it ('TASTES LIKE COUGH SYRUP'); then a top-down F1 car on a white page between blue vertical bars, bars standing as lane markings. Product is the one cutout, colours pulled from the can (blue, red, white)
why_it_works: palette lifted from the product label makes every scene feel branded without a logo wall

finding: Window-in-wallpaper transition: small OS windows open on the green hills ('it became a fifty billion dollar empire' typed in a title bar) with a photo-in-window, buttons with red close; next beat hard cut to black for 'AND SOMEHOW'. Dialog windows stack at 3 sizes
why_it_works: windows are a native layering device and give the screen a depth stack
use_when: stacking evidence over a soft ground

finding: Mid-sentence layout: 'WHAT'S INSIDE THE CAN' over a thin-corner-frame viewfinder with the can centred, thin-sans text with caps in the title; 'BECAUSE OF WHAT THE CAN MEANS' typed in condensed white on deep navy. Corner brackets mark the focus area and are 4 corner ticks of ~30px
why_it_works: viewfinder brackets hold the eye on the object
use_when: a close inspection of a product

finding: Sports-footage montage with oversized brand marks: bull logo big and cropped, blue-white split background with words 'SPEED', 'RISK', 'ADRENALINE' stacking in and sliding off; F1 pan blur with lens streaks; cliff diver clip with web address; skydiver from space. Words alternate left/right on the split so the layout reads as a ping-pong
why_it_works: split-colour ground gives a built-in two-column rhythm for the words
use_when: a trio of attributes next to footage

finding: Circular diagram on cream: ring with labels 'THE CAFFEINE', 'THE SUGAR', 'THE PACKAGING' on small brown plates around it, then centre statement 'NOBODY COULD COPY THE FEELING'; next a maroon slate with a shopping cart containing the can, teddy and bags tilted 20deg with a bold line 'PEOPLE DON'T BUY PRODUCTS'. Diagram plates are all equal and rest on the ring
why_it_works: equal plates around a ring show interchangeable parts, the centre is the one thing left

finding: Ending slows to a long hold: B&W-graded person against mountains with a caption lower-left, a skier cut, then black with 'AND THAT CHANGES EVERYTHING' held about 1.5s and the site name held about 2s. Shots 25 stepped, but the final 3s are three static slates
why_it_works: a still end lets the CTA be read and the energy settle

finding: Hero-word-first layout: huge red condensed 'COSTCO GIVES AWAY' sits above a grey B&W storefront; then 'FREE FOOD EVERY SINGLE DAY' in the same red over white with a waiter's gloved hand lowering a silver cloche that lifts to a burger (3D props, hand cutout from the right edge). Red is the only colour in a grey scene, so the headline is the colour
why_it_works: a desaturated plate with one red headline makes type the subject
use_when: a headline over a place photo

finding: Word-search puzzle on red: rows of letter grid with a small black sticker cursor, the word 'GENEROSITY' is picked out by the letters highlighting; then a glass case with sample bottles and an orange line chart climbing over them ('TWO THOUSAND PERCENT' in gold 3D letters). Chart line draws in 8 steps; stepped playback
why_it_works: grid + highlight is the data viz for a hidden word

finding: Ribbons swirl: pink, lime and orange ribbons with text ('PSYCHOLOGY', 'NOTHING TO DO', 'FOOD') sweep across a dark ground, crossing each other at ~30deg, then cut to a sky with gold 'RECIPROCITY' small caps; the ribbon is the transition and the text rides it
why_it_works: text on a moving band reads as a swipe transition and a title at once
use_when: concept intro with a list of words

finding: Object-per-line: 'SOMEONE GIVES YOU SOMETHING FOR FREE' written on a spiral notepad in teal marker-block letters on a teal ground; laptop with a pink slab and dialog 'AN UNCONSCIOUS OBLIGATION' in a dialog; a cube of cheese in gold 3D on black ('ONE SMALL CUBE OF CHEESE') with a spotlight. 3D props are glossy and sharp, each on its own colour ground
why_it_works: glossy 3D props pop from flat grounds and make a plain line concrete
use_when: the line names a physical thing

finding: Top-down shopping cart on orange: hands from the bottom push the cart toward the camera, text 'YOU'RE WALKING OUT' tracks above it and sub-line 'SOMETHING YOU NEVER PLANNED TO BUY' appears below, then a hard cut to the real storefront. Hands on the handle enter from the bottom edge and give a first-person viewpoint
why_it_works: first-person hands make the viewer the shopper

finding: Statistic scenes: '$46 billion' in green money-print letters over a banknote image on greige; ring progress '17%' counting on black with a gold arc; 'ENTIRE REVENUE.' typed word by word; end punch 'IT WAS ALWAYS FREE' where 'FREE' is orange, replacing 'WAS NEVER SALE' in place. Final word swapped in place in orange
why_it_works: in-place word swap gives the twist the voice says
use_when: a punch line replaces a prior word

finding: Top-down football pitch: years scroll up the grass '1930 1929 ...' while boots enter from the top and a ball rolls in (ball in the same position, years track behind); then a crowd-of-faces mosaic behind a spinning ball with 'EXPERIMENT' label; a figure standing at the centre circle under 'FEW BELIEVED WOULD LAST', camera pulling out 1.0 to 0.85 over 1.2s. Overhead consistently on pitch scenes
why_it_works: top-down keeps the type-on-ground layout and treats the field as a page
use_when: a sport or map scene where text sits on the ground

finding: Sky scene: an airplane flies across clouds as red '13 TEAMS' slides in with birds; next a vintage map of Uruguay with planes and cloud banks overlay and a yellow tape label 'COMPETE IN THE' on top. Clouds enter as foreground layers on both sides, closing over the previous scene
why_it_works: clouds are a free wipe that fits the travel line

finding: Wood-desk top-down with trophies and flags: country cards (Spain, England, Germany) with a 'DECLINED' red stamp slap onto the table, a yellow label 'THE LONG JOURNEY ACROSS THE ATLANTIC' pins above; stack of cards 3 deep with a different rotation each. Stamp lands with scale from 1.3 to 1.0 in 2 frames
why_it_works: stamp landing is the percussive beat

finding: Archive-to-modern cut series: close-ups of the trophy kissed, B&W old footage, game footage with a blue-green tint; each clip is 0.7s and the caption sits at the bottom in thin white; 'NEARLY A CENTURY LATER' in red pixel font on black marks the time jump. Footage clips are colour-graded to the same teal/gold
why_it_works: one grade over mixed footage keeps it a single world
use_when: montage of archive and current footage

finding: Earth on black with landmark cutouts (Statue of Liberty, Pisa tower, pyramid) growing from the globe, clouds rolling; then trophy in the centre of a stadium tunnel, jerseys facing away. End logo lock-up: gold trophy with the 'FIFA World Cup' wordmark in white, held 1s on black, then yellow slate 'VISIT NOW AND DOWNLOAD IT' in glowing outline type
why_it_works: black ground and gold trophy form a clean lock-up

finding: Price-tag scene built as a stage: a spotlit popcorn bucket in a blue circular spot on dark navy; price tag on the bucket changes in steps ($6.00 to $9.00 to $8.50) while the bucket slides left and a second bucket enters; then a yellow slate with red 'SUDDENLY' where the $9.00 bucket rises from the bottom. Spotlight circle is ~70% of frame width, tag sits at bucket mid-height
why_it_works: spotlight isolates the product, price swap in place makes the argument without words
use_when: a numeric comparison on one object

finding: Green felt desk top-down: three kraft-paper price cards ($3.50, $8.00 in the middle, $9.00) each with a popcorn bucket cutout, Game Boy, controller, Netflix/Amazon tags and a dollar bill scattered; the middle card slides to centre when 'IN THE MIDDLE' types. Three-card comparison where the middle option is physically placed between the two others
why_it_works: physical layout equals the idea (middle option)

finding: Cloud-sky ground with a $9.00 bucket, gold gradient type 'MAKE THE EXPENSIVE FEEL SMARTER' in 3D gold-yellow with white outline and drop shadow; next, Steve Jobs photo with white caps 'APPLE DOES IT WITH STORAGE UPGRADES' crossing his body, cut on the beat. Two gold/white outline styles used: gold for the concept, white for facts
why_it_works: colour code of text style = role of the line

finding: Rotated film-strip pattern: a diagonal grid of red film strips fills the frame rotating slowly (30deg) with a label 'MOVIE THEATRE' on a red stamp that scales in; the stamp flips to 'FOR DECADES' and then a starburst '1' appears. Strip field is the ground, type is on top; label swap occurs in the same place
why_it_works: patterned moving ground is energy; the stable label box keeps it readable

finding: Frame-on-wall ending: gold picture frames hang on maroon wallpaper; 'MADE THE SMART DECISION' fills the frame label by label (3 steps) and the next scene is a brick wall with a phone on a plate and a green name tag, closing with a magenta slate 'VISIT NOW AND DOWNLOAD IT' typed. Brick and wallpaper are the only wall textures in the piece
why_it_works: museum frame turns the last line into a trophy; the ending slate changes ground to a loud pink to mark the CTA

finding: 13 hold shots in 39 and 23 soft transitions; the piece runs a call-and-response between a prop scene (1-2s) and a single-line type slate (0.5-1s). 'THAT WAS NEVER AN ACCIDENT' red-on-black slate lasts about 1.2s before the space scene 'IT'S CALLED DECOY EFFECT'
why_it_works: slate after a scene lets the line land, the prop scene after a slate refreshes the eye

style: spotlight props, kraft cards, film strips

finding: Surreal photographed tableau: gingham picnic tablecloth running into a formal garden, burger, fries and two cans lined across it; the lower third carries a thin caption line; then floating land chunks (like a cut piece of garden turf) in lilac clouds each holding one food item ('IT DOESN'T SELL' over burger, soda, chips). Items on islands = 'one object per island' composition
why_it_works: island with one object reads as a specimen, the cloud ground gives space around it

finding: Orange label bars with black type 'IT'S A WEEKLY INJECTION' slide in from the left (bar grows first, text follows) on black; later 'OZEMPIC WAS ORIGINALLY DESIGNED' on a CRT monitor with green/pink sticky notes that update word by word as 'DESIGNED TO TREAT DIABETES'; the sticky notes are tiny mock UI chips. Orange bar leads, text follows after 2-3 frames
why_it_works: bar before text anticipates the word and focuses the area

finding: Store-aisle and queue photo with a hand holding a protest sign entering from the bottom ('NOT BECAUSE OF DISCIPLINE.'), white sign on dark background; then a clipboard on a locker-grey ground where handwriting types in script ('the drug chemically changed their appetite'). Hand-held signs and clipboards act as text carriers inside real photos
why_it_works: text on a physical carrier in the photo keeps the photo as the scene
use_when: a sign/line within a documentary photo

finding: Burned-in caption band at the lower 8% on every photo scene (white thin sans, one phrase) plus a separate hero text only where there is a graphic; stock-style clips (kale chips bags, protein chips, gloved hands, beer bottle on ice) shown 1.2-1.5s each in a rapid list, each with a caption change on the cut
why_it_works: caption and clip change together so the list item is clear
use_when: a quick list over stock footage

finding: Newspaper clipping 'DAILY NEWS' on a flat red ground: clipping is slightly rotated (3deg), cream paper with serif body; the sheet enters from the right and slides left over 4 frames; the text of the stat remains small (the caption carries the sentence). Red ground makes the paper stand out
why_it_works: newspaper cutout on one flat colour is credibility shorthand
use_when: citing a source or a stat

finding: Small thin type on black and white slates: 'ONE PHARMACEUTICAL DRUG DIDN'T JUST DISRUPT HEALTHCARE' in about 1.5% of frame height centred on a huge empty ground; this is too small for a phone and only works because the caption repeats it. Better pieces make the key line 8-12% of the height
why_it_works: readability at phone size needs at least about 5% height for key lines
use_when: avoid on any line that carries the idea

finding: Every beat is a new full-bleed 'set' with one hero object and one headline: striped fabric + cut-out man, newspaper on wood desk, green lockers + paper poster, clipboard on white tile, orange flat. Background changes its material per idea (fabric, paper, metal, tile, flat colour) so each line reads as a new place, not a new slide.
why_it_works: material change = chapter change; the viewer never has to read a layout, only one object
use_when: each narration sentence introduces a new idea or actor

finding: Counter prop: a flip-board number '30' sits at the figure's belt, ticks to '33' and a blue 'YEARS OLD' plate slides in under it while the cut-out man holds still. The data is a physical object in the scene, not a caption.
why_it_works: number change is the motion; figure stays stable so the eye follows the delta
use_when: a number or age or count changes in the line

finding: Newspaper scene: the page is oversized (bleeds off two sides), tilted ~10 deg on a wood-grain desk, slow rotate + drift; a yellow marker band highlights the key phrase and the photo is B&W halftone. Frame is cropped so only half the page shows.
why_it_works: cropping and tilt give scale and a hand-held feel; marker colour is the only accent
use_when: quoting or proving with a document

finding: Hard swap from the paper-collage world to photoreal cinematic footage (leather bag, archive shelves) with a giant blurred-out title word passing over the bag; the two worlds are bridged by a letterform scaling through, not by a dissolve.
why_it_works: one oversized word acts as the wipe; no cross-fade needed
use_when: switching from stylised to documentary footage

finding: Type is bold condensed sans, white or red on flat colour (orange, green), set tight and stacked 2-3 lines; the word that carries the turn is swapped by a yellow tape/label or red-to-yellow recolour (e.g. 'IT SAID YES TO EVERYTHING' on a yellow strip over a clipboard). Words build one at a time, line grows by word.
why_it_works: word-by-word build matches speech; label colour contrast marks the key phrase

finding: Posterized motion: 21 of 32 shots are 'stepped' (held frames ~every 2-3 frames) so even slow drifts read as stop-motion paper; shots are mostly slow drift/pull-out over 1.4 s with an initial brief hold.
why_it_works: stepping hides the digital smoothness and sells the paper material
use_when: any camera move over collage plates

finding: Outro promo: phone mockup on red gingham picnic cloth over grass, text typing in the screen. Same collage language as the story, so the ad does not break the style.
why_it_works: CTA uses a real-world prop scene in the piece's own register

finding: Scenes are tabletop-from-above or sky sets: retro Mac floating over grass with sky; red felt with playing cards; teal sky; green felt with laptop cut-outs, crumpled paper balls, paperclips, earbuds. Props are scattered at varied scale and rotation around a central subject, leaving the middle clear for the headline.
why_it_works: clutter at the edges frames a calm centre; scale variety gives depth
use_when: desk/tabletop scene that must hold a headline

finding: Red condensed headline with white stroke and drop shadow sits behind the object (the Mac occludes the word's bottom), then the word rebuilds in front. Layering text between plates (behind hero, in front of sky) creates depth with no 3D.
why_it_works: occlusion = depth cue

finding: Five consecutive micro-shots of ~0.13 s each (shots 7-11) as a pull-out burst, then a 2 s hold. The burst = a quick snap-zoom out as a wipe from black 'NVIDIA JUST CHANGED THAT' to the sky.
why_it_works: rapid micro-beats read as one energetic transition, then silence resets
use_when: a hook line followed by the body

finding: Phone mock-up scene: camera starts close on the screen text (heavy crop, perspective-skewed), then pull-out reveals the whole phone on red felt; zoom 0.61-0.82. The UI is real readable content, not blur.
why_it_works: close-up proves the source, pull-out gives context and centres the device
use_when: showing a screenshot or article as proof

finding: Colour-flat background swaps between scenes: white with black stacked type, orange with dark chat bar, black with yellow/orange highlighted words. Pulling type in word by word, with highlight word recoloured to yellow/orange and a small paper-fold arrow accent beside it.

measure.palette: red, teal, green, white, orange, black

why_it_works: each beat gets its own flat colour so the cut is felt even with the same typeface

finding: Backgrounds are woven fabric/felt/linen textures with visible grain (red felt, green felt, orange canvas) rather than flat vectors; props cast soft shadows. Saturated one-colour fields: one dominant colour per scene.
why_it_works: texture + shadow ground cut-outs on a surface

finding: Hero is a single photoreal full-body or half-body figure cut out and placed centred on a graded environment; the same person is shown in colour (sky, brand sign) when the line is about the peak and in desaturated B&W with a dark vignette when the line is about the fall. Colour vs B&W carries the emotion.
why_it_works: one subject, two grades, no extra graphics needed to say 'before/after'
use_when: a rise-and-fall narrative on one person

finding: Portrait starts small inside an ornate gold frame hung on a grey wall, then the frame grows to fill the screen in ~1.5 s (pull-in) and the person breaks out of the frame into the street scene. Frame = entrance device that also becomes the transition.
why_it_works: the container expands into the scene; no cut needed
use_when: introducing a subject and then going into their story

finding: Captions are lower-case-style serif italic (light, thin) set small over the image at chest height, one or two words at a time, built word by word, with a soft shadow; a few big words use a bold serif ('Forty-five billion') in cream. No highlighter, no boxes. Quiet, magazine-like.
why_it_works: type stays out of the photo's way; hierarchy by size and weight only

finding: Dense pile of newspaper clippings on dark wood, each rotated differently, overlapping with soft shadows; camera hovers over the pile with shallow depth of field (edges blurred, centre sharp) and pans; headline '25 MILLION' sits in the centre clipping.
why_it_works: depth of field puts focus on the one clipping that matters
use_when: a pile of evidence, one key figure

finding: Red logo on black spreads into vertical colour stripes (a bar/glitch burst: red to rainbow gradient stripes), then cuts to flat cream paper with italic 'What changed.' A colour-bar burst is the chapter break between 'fall' and 'recovery'.
why_it_works: abstract colour burst resets the eye between two worlds
use_when: a pivot in the story ('then everything changed')

finding: B&W cut-out figure walks the camera: scenes are 2D plates with slow pull-out + slight rotate (z 0.9-1.0), background out of focus; mid-scene the person is blurred with a motion smear in cut 17 when a swap occurs. Posters on the wall appear one after another as small framed props.
why_it_works: blur-on-swap hides the plate change
use_when: re-using one figure across several beats

finding: Licensed show stills (colour, hard crop on the face, small centred title in thin serif) break the grey grade; they work because they are cropped extreme close-up and held 1 s each, so colour pops as the payoff.
why_it_works: colour only for the payoff images
use_when: showing the things that made the change

finding: Fastest piece of the batch: 8.4 events/10s, ASL 1.15 s, with 12 of 30 shots rotating and 12 panning. Beats are one word or one object each; the 'TWENTY BILLION' word is built in 2 steps (TWENTY, then BILLION) on a swap of background colour, white to black to lime.
why_it_works: every spoken number or noun gets its own picture, so image and voice stay locked

finding: Cut-out money-filled green pillow floats above a wooden stool on a pale grid paper, with a small cloud and distant hill: surreal object, one accent colour (lime green) + black type. Type sits above the object, small yellow star burst marks the hit.
why_it_works: one odd object plus one accent colour makes the idea memorable

finding: Hard cut from one world to the next with a blur-out: the end of a shot is a heavy zoom/motion-blur frame (cut 1 frame +1 shows horizontal smear), the next shot opens already settled. Used between lime title, red OFFER set, and the CEO portrait.
why_it_works: 1 frame of smear hides the swap and adds energy
use_when: fast hard cuts between unrelated plates

finding: Portrait cut with a torn-paper hole edge: the man's photo shows through a ripped aperture in a brown wood/leather ground, torn white fibre edge visible, big stroked 'NVIDIA' word skewed across it with a red scribble line; then spins/blurs (rotation + blur) into the next shot.
why_it_works: torn rim reads as a physical cut-out so the photo sits in the paper, not on it
use_when: revealing a portrait inside a collage

finding: Icon-style vector gags (green spiral funnel, row of white people icons dropping, yellow sun burst rays rotating behind the word 'conviction', then rays morph into a clock face) share one flat black ground and bright primary fills. Shapes morph into each other by position, not by dissolve.
why_it_works: one shape becomes the next, continuity without cuts
use_when: abstract idea sequence ('what X looks like')

finding: Yellow label with black text ('not because') pinned bottom-third over the speaking portrait as a highlighter plate; the big 2008 numeral sits behind the person's shoulders (person occludes the digits). Same device in DZXDJ8AuAiU (yellow strip).
why_it_works: numeral behind subject = depth, yellow label = annotation
use_when: person on camera needing a date and a short claim

finding: Colour palette per scene is hard-limited to two hues plus black/white: red + black for the offer, lime + black for money, brown wood + white, blue sky + grey. Footage clips (ocean, robot) appear desaturated with one thin text caption.
why_it_works: limited palette makes disparate assets sit together

finding: Each scene is built from one theme-matched world: grass+sky (scientist figure with date plates), blue desk with Game Boy and B&W portrait, wood desk with graph paper and a cassette tape, red wall with gold frame, bookcase with a hand holding playing cards. The portrait is always B&W halftone, the props are colour; props are period-coded objects (cassette = 1774).
why_it_works: colour props around a grey face puts the eye on the face and the prop tells the era

finding: Numerals appear as separate paper plates that flip into place ('1771' built from tiled cards), then the cut-out figure holds a speech-bubble banner that bends and swings in; small objects bounce in with overshoot while the figure stays fixed.
why_it_works: background elements animate, figure is the stable anchor

finding: Stacked bold condensed headline built one line per beat on flat colour: red on black ('NEITHER / PUBLISHED / FIRST'), dark green on mustard ('BEING FIRST DOESN'T GUARANTEE CREDIT'), mustard on green. Last word is oversize or recoloured. Each slide is a flat colour card with no image: the pause between image scenes.
why_it_works: flat colour type cards are the sentence break, easy to read

finding: Overhead desk scene with slow drift and subtle perspective tilt; the cassette tape number rolls ('1','17','177','1774') as a counter on the label, graph paper has torn bottom edge and a window-shadow overlay moving across it. Info cards (polaroid + small body text + red name) are added in 3 steps and the layout shifts by zoom-out each time.
why_it_works: zoom-out makes room for each new card; shadows give a sense of daylight
use_when: adding facts about the same subject

finding: Black cut-through: a one-frame black between the dark-red frame scene and the TV scene (cut 12 frame -1 is black). Scene boundaries mostly hard cuts, sometimes with a 1-frame black or a blur frame; no dissolves.
why_it_works: hard cuts keep pace
use_when: scene change in a cut-out piece

finding: A red scribble drawn over the portrait inside the gold frame (hand-drawn S-curve loop in red) as an annotation; the frame has a visible dark gap shadow on a red wall with a dust texture. Frame = a physical prop that holds the face.
why_it_works: hand-scribble over a clean cutout adds imperfection

finding: Outro Game Boy floats on sky with typed green LCD text. Same promo device as Dacjr7jNsbG (browser card) and DZXDJ8AuAiU (phone on gingham): the CTA is always a prop scene.
why_it_works: CTA stays in style

finding: Highest event rate of the pieces so far: 10.9 events/10s, ASL 0.9 s (shots as short as 0.2 s). Many events are word swaps in a flat type card ('NOT BY A COMPETITOR' builds as coloured highlight bars with each word wiped in) rather than image changes.
why_it_works: word-level beats keep attention in a text-heavy story

finding: Open: dark warm ground, centred starburst logo with hands reaching up from below (low-key, orange glow). Then high-key: striped orange/cream wall with 'BANNED' stamp held by a hand, egg with cracking shell and the orange asterisk hatching out. Palette per scene is two warm hues; objects centred with a lot of empty ground.
why_it_works: one brand colour carries the whole story

finding: Newspaper masthead page ('Fake Times') filling the screen: small justified serif body text with yellow highlight sweep on the key clause, then the logo mark bursting through the page. Fake documents used as proof pages with highlighter.
why_it_works: highlighter = reading cursor

finding: Fast logo/brand flash run: Gemini, a bird logo, jasper, 'Hey Copilot,' each on a plain white or dark card for ~0.3 s, then a word-search grid page. Neutral card per brand so the brand is the only content.
why_it_works: a rapid list as a rhythm roll

finding: Hazard 'SHUT DOWN' sign on yellow/black tape; mousetrap with the logo on it; a face with spiky rays behind it (sunburst) spinning slowly; rocket moving across starfield. Each object has a single idle motion (spin, bob) while text builds.
why_it_works: idle motion keeps a held image alive

finding: Text often overlaps objects awkwardly ('EVENING' / 'COLLAPSED' running through a rocket; type clipped at frame edge while sliding). It reads as energetic because the clip is only 0.3 s; held longer it would look wrong.
why_it_works: overlap only tolerated for sub-second beats
use_when: avoid on any hold above 1 s

finding: Promo: yellow bold wordmark types in letter by letter on black, then the site card slides up from the bottom with the cursor drawing a line. Same end card across the account.
why_it_works: consistent outro

finding: Story is told with B&W halftone photos on neutral grey/white paper with one accent colour per object (yellow marker underline and label, red Ferrari key and shield, red car, red caption plate). Colour appears only on the brand objects, so the rivalry reads as red vs grey.
why_it_works: photographic people are all grey, brand objects carry the colour

finding: Cut-out figure with a thick cream outline (sticker rim) and a halo outline around a speech label 'One Insult' that overlaps his legs; figure sits on a tractor, car behind. Halftone dots visible across the photo. The outline unifies photos of different quality.
why_it_works: the rim makes the cut crisp on any ground
use_when: pasting a photo cut-out onto a busy scene

finding: Captions are serif italic with a yellow marker underline or a highlighter highlight on the key word ('Ferruccio Lamborghini' underlined as a name tag at the bottom of the portrait; 'Clutch' on a yellow sticky label with a hand-drawn circle around the pedals). Type is shown as hand annotation on the object.
why_it_works: annotation inside the image keeps the eye on the picture
use_when: labeling a part of an image

finding: Photos enter as rounded-corner polaroid-like tiles on black, slightly rotated (~8 deg), one replacing another with a 1-2 frame tilt-swap; a typewriter caption (yellow serif) types below. Rounded tile on pure black = a clean gallery frame.
why_it_works: consistent tile shape unifies archive photos

finding: Mono typewriter type on pale grey: 'that's / How / one / insult' as a big stacked text card between photo sequences; a plain text card acts as chapter beat. Type in a different family (mono) than the serif captions marks the thesis.
why_it_works: typeface switch flags the punchline

finding: Cut-out car drives across a horizon strip on a pale page with sky above, built as a 3-band layout (sky, road strip, text band). The red car is the single saturated item. A walking man cut-out is animated with a step-cycle (two poses alternating) over a brick facade.
why_it_works: two-pose swaps give a paper-puppet walk cheaply
use_when: a person has to move across the frame

finding: Outro: hand holding phone on green desk with headphones, keyboard and camera as props, After Effects icon stickers pop in, yellow label types 'AFTER EFFECT PROJECT', then a flat yellow card with the wordmark. Hand and desk props from a photo, stylised with the same halftone.
why_it_works: same prop language as the story

finding: Extreme event rate: 39.5 events/10s, ASL 0.25 s over 1:1 frames. Each beat is one word or syllable on a new layout (rotated block, spiral of letters, stripe grid), so the piece reads as a type-driven beat edit, not narrated explainer. Black/white/red + one accent green or gold, same figure silhouette repeats.
why_it_works: events land on beats; limited palette keeps the chaos readable
use_when: music-led hook or montage, not narrated explainers

finding: Letters are treated as objects: spiralling around the figure in a spotlight cone, spun on a circle path, falling into the frame, or broken across white/black stripes (R-E-M / D-E-A-S letters in black/white checks). Words pass behind the silhouette (occluded by the figure) to place type in the scene.
why_it_works: type as scenery, not caption

finding: Transitions are carried by colour floods: green fills the frame, a white diagonal bar sweeps, a grey block wipes, then a red square panel arrives. Each is a flat colour plate used as a wipe that is also the next scene's background.
why_it_works: wipe becomes the next ground, no wasted frames

finding: Faceless figures: the head is replaced by a smeared brown/golden texture, a white blank, or a crown of rays; a lone small silhouette stands in a pool of light with huge empty black around it. Scale contrast (tiny figure, huge type) and total black negative space give the drama.
why_it_works: small figure in black reads as lonely, no face needed

finding: Type is often cropped by the frame, overlapped by the figure or by another word (GROUND / D, SUCCESS overlapped by hands), which only reads because each beat lasts 0.25-0.5 s and is repeated by the music; on an explainer these overlaps would be illegible.
why_it_works: legibility rule is relaxed only at sub-second holds
use_when: do not transfer to narrated explainers

finding: Lyric-style kinetic type on a 1:1 frame: words stretch ('LESSOOOOOON' stretched until it fills the width), type sits inside a speech bubble that gets squashed, or letters fall in as separate tiles; a social-post card ('Peter Parker ... I'm never like thisssss') is typed live and the S's keep growing. Words stretch to the duration of the sung syllable.
why_it_works: type length = audio length; viewer reads rhythm

finding: Hard palette: red, white, navy blue and black, taken from the character's costume; every frame has red as the dominant. Halftone / web line-art overlays, torn-paper rims on photo panels, spider web strokes as graphic texture. Background alternates paper-white and black to give contrast between beats.
why_it_works: palette from the subject, not the editor

finding: Full-frame red slab wipes in as a trapezoid (diagonal edge) and becomes the ground for the next word ('MAN,'); the slab then breaks into shards that scatter and expose the next scene. Same wipe-into-ground move as DausEm8OxlC.
why_it_works: shape change doubles as next layout

finding: Close-up of a single eye fills the frame (cut-in to the mask's lens glowing), then a stylised mask with white cross-hatched shards behind it. The close-up gives a quiet frame between loud text beats.
why_it_works: extreme scale jump is the focal beat
use_when: emotional peak in a type montage

finding: Film-still panels with white keylines and a drop shadow are stacked at different angles, one cut-out figure hanging upside-down from a web over a city skyline with cloud sky photo; panels overlap type ('HOW / THAT'S MY LIFE') so type goes behind one panel and over the next.
why_it_works: mixed layering gives magazine-spread depth
use_when: collage of stills with a headline

finding: End card on black: two AE icon stickers rotate at corners and a small 'Comment Link' line types in. Simple and legible after chaos.
why_it_works: quiet last frame

finding: 16:9 typography-only motion piece: small centred sans-serif (about 4-5% of frame height) on white or black, with one word enlarged and blurred-glowed in red ('Risk', 'Simple' with a cyan glow) and letters smearing in/out horizontally. Emoji and small product icons orbit the text. Black gets a different mood to white.
why_it_works: huge empty frame and tiny type = calm, premium; one coloured word carries the stress

finding: Colour-flood transitions: a blue gradient sweeps up from the bottom and fills the frame, brand mark appears centred inside ripple rings; the same blue becomes the end card. Sweep also hides the text swap.
why_it_works: brand colour as wipe and as destination

finding: Emoji art (baby, money, angry face) is a different art style from the product icons and clip-art look cheap against the clean type; it only reads as intentional because it moves fast. Better pieces keep one object style per scene.
why_it_works: consistent object style

finding: 16:9 collage explainer. Scenes are built as a repeating pattern ground (pattern of retro computers on black, wall of open-mouth stickers with white die-cut rims) with one off-pattern hero in the centre ('Computer Revolution' yellow tape label X-ed out; one sticker mouth scaled bigger). Pattern = texture, hero = the only thing that breaks it.
why_it_works: repetition makes the odd one out instantly findable
use_when: showing a crowd, a market, a category

finding: Real footage is shown inside a rounded-corner white-bordered card that shrinks from full-bleed to a framed window on pale paper, with subtitle line under the card; ends in a flat UI card ('KH-MouthPad Connected'). Footage enters the collage world by shrinking into a frame instead of cutting to a different look.
why_it_works: frame = same material as the rest of the paper world

finding: Kaleidoscope zoom burst: the frame is mirrored into a radial symmetrical pattern with heavy radial motion blur (~1 shot), then resolves into the studio set. The burst is the cut between the footage and the cut-out set.
why_it_works: symmetry burst resets composition
use_when: jump from footage to cut-out stage

finding: Stage set: three seated people cut out and centred on pale grey ground between studio lights and film cameras (symmetric, small hero group ~25% of height), hand-drawn red annotations over each head ('paralysis'). A black chalkboard card slides in below and types the line in white handwriting, yellow keyline, red circle on the key word. Annotation language = pen, chalk, tape.
why_it_works: symmetry plus empty space makes room for the chalkboard

finding: Marionette in a red theatre proscenium: the figure is a small cut-out under strings in a white stage box, framed by red curtains and carved columns; a slow zoom-in toward the stage on each beat. Frame-in-frame gives a point of focus and negative space.
why_it_works: a strongly framed stage keeps the tiny figure the centre

finding: Serif italic typing with a yellow cursor on grey paper ('What if the next ...') opens the film; no image yet. Type cursor + typed words = the narration appears as it is spoken. Also in Da2XkSfOy7h (italic serif) and DafS1lPu18x (typewriter).
why_it_works: type reveal doubles as the first beat

finding: Closing: black chalkboard on graph-paper desk (ruler, pen, torn paper) and 3 AE file icons pop in, a yellow label sweeps over them and spells the site. Props on the desk are static; only the label animates.
why_it_works: outro is quiet

finding: Open on a sky-and-cloud wallpaper with a big yellow number ('31 years') popping on, then the toy characters stand on a strip of sand at the bottom third: full-bleed ground, a ground line at 1/3, characters sized ~35% of height, title logo above them. The ground colour is the film's own sky.
why_it_works: the ground is the world of the film, immediate recognition

finding: Black bars wipe in across the sky as a horizontal band; a circular iris hole shows the sky/clouds, the title 'Biggest franchise' is set in a bold yellow serif inside the band. The iris opens with a shape-mask reveal. Hero flies across with a motion smear before the wipe.
why_it_works: iris = film language for focus

finding: A marquee-bulb-framed poster on a dark wall pushes in, the box-office number '312' builds on the poster, then the frame cuts to a macro extreme close-up of a banknote portrait that slowly pushes. Macro of the dollar bill, with halftone grain, is the money metaphor with no text.
why_it_works: one metaphor image holds for the line

finding: Pixar logo letter blocks drop/stack onto a green bench (letters as red dice-like cubes) and a gloved hand with a wand wipes through the word, erasing it ('FOR YEARS' becomes 'NOT YEARS'); hand/wand is the agent that changes the text.
why_it_works: a visible hand makes text edits feel physical

finding: Mood shift told by grade: dark cavern/brown wood walls with a spotlight on a framed poster ('Fade with Time' in yellow serif on wood panel), then warm saturated film frames of the toys. Dark = past, warm = payoff.
why_it_works: grade carries the tone
use_when: fall then recovery in the same piece

finding: Type is mostly yellow (#f0d020-like) bold serif or condensed on the scene's ground, with a white italic serif for thin lines; an oval hand-drawn ring marks a phrase on a white card. Yellow is the consistent accent across the account (also in DafS1lPu18x, DZXDJ8AuAiU).
why_it_works: one accent colour per account makes pieces identifiable

finding: Film stills are all soft and halftoned the same way (visible dot screen) so licensed 3D frames sit in the same material as the paper plates. Without the screen, they would look pasted on.
why_it_works: one texture across all sources

finding: Same Netflix story as Da2XkSfOy7h, shown with the AE interface visible: the cut-out figures are flat plates with 3D layer gizmos and the camera move is a few-keyframe push toward the subject (timeline shows 2-3 keyframes per move). The move is a slow scale-in of the whole plate, with a deep push to an extreme face close-up (cut 4-5: full body to face in ~1 shot) as a punch-in.
why_it_works: the extreme close-up is a one-shot emphasis; no other effect
use_when: the line is an emotion or a quote from one person

finding: The photoreal 'room' is a generated bookcase interior with a spot of light from a lamp (a cone of cream light added as a layer), the person seated behind a table with banknote stacks that are recoloured lime green when the money line is spoken; a spotlight cone and a colour change on the prop direct the eye.
why_it_works: recolouring the one prop is the emphasis; the rest stays muted
use_when: calling out one object in a photoreal plate

finding: Words are big serif italic cream with the key word ('billion') scaled 2-3x larger in a heavier weight, stacked in three lines left-aligned to the figure's silhouette so the type hugs the person; yellow underline sweep under the key phrase on dark B&W plates ('of the end').
why_it_works: scale contrast inside one line sets hierarchy without colour
use_when: statements with one number or word

finding: Blur-swap between plates: the old shot de-focuses (heavy gaussian) one frame before the swap, the new shot is born already sharp (cut 22 frames). Same device in DaAV2R5IuSi and Da2XkSfOy7h.
why_it_works: consistent cheap transition

finding: Dup / near-dup of Da2XkSfOy7h with the AE UI left in; use only the AE panels for how the timeline is built (few layers per scene, 2-3 keyframes per move). Nothing else new.
why_it_works: n/a

finding: Tabletop on grid paper (flat-lay, camera straight down): product bottles at the left, pill/toothbrush props around, syringe hanging from the top, handwritten oval around the word 'Antiseptic' and a yellow label; wide margins and cool grey ground; everything casts a soft shadow. Lays out props at varied angles with the key product low-centre.
why_it_works: flat-lay with consistent top light and shadow reads as a table
use_when: introducing a product and its context

finding: Shape-mask iris zoom: a pentagon grows from small to full-frame (crimson), a hexagon opens inside it, then a circle opens and shows the next scene (a bottle in a library) through the hole, growing until it fills the frame. A chain of scale-up shapes passes the viewer into the next world: each shape is the mask and the colour ground.
why_it_works: geometry sequence is a match-cut tunnel into the next scene
use_when: opening a chapter or entering a past era

finding: Yellow sticky notes slap onto the bottle photo one after another with staggered timing, each carrying 2-3 words of narration, rotated at slightly different angles (±5 deg) and overlapping; new notes push older ones off. Notes = captions as objects.
why_it_works: stagger builds the sentence and reads as handwriting on a desk

finding: Iceberg metaphor: small petri-dish detail as a labelled magnified circle ('Product') tops an iceberg, the huge underwater part labelled 'problem' in a yellow tag; two-thirds of the frame is the dark teal underwater area. Scale = the idea, with labels tied by thin lines.
why_it_works: the picture itself shows the ratio

finding: Overhead scan of a medical page: camera slowly pans/pushes, a yellow highlighter pen sits in the top corner and sweeps a yellow band over the headline word (halitosis); a marker ring around the page. The prop that does the highlighting stays in frame.
why_it_works: the pen on screen justifies the highlight
use_when: emphasising a word in a document

finding: Handwritten chalk-style script 'convincing people' scales in from a motion blur over a photoreal person (smear horizontally to sharp in 2 frames, white with soft glow) while small serif subtitles remain at the bottom: two layers of type, big expressive for the key phrase and small neutral for the running subtitle.
why_it_works: separates emphasis from reading text
use_when: person-on-camera plate with an emphasised phrase

finding: Chart built from product bottles standing as bars (growing stack) in a frame on desk; number '$1 million' in serif with a red pen oval and a yellow tape under it, then the final text 'In just six years' typed one letter at a time on blank grid paper. The graph is made of the actual product, not an abstract chart.
why_it_works: object-as-data

finding: Every scene has a distinct colour family (white grid paper; orange to crimson to green shapes; wood library; deep teal night; cream newspaper; grey office; white desk), scenes never mix more than two saturated hues, with a halftone dot layer on all of them to unify.
why_it_works: distinct ground per beat, halftone = glue

finding: Photoreal staged tableaux with a hero figure at 40-60% of frame height, one clear setting per idea (cinema lobby with poster, stage with spotlights and a blurred crowd of raised hands at the bottom foreground, retro 'Galaxy Theatre' marquee with a row of people looking at phones, Roman soldier at a map table, study with lamp). Foreground blur (hands, silhouettes) frames the hero and gives depth.
why_it_works: a foreground blur layer, a sharp midground and a background make depth without 3D

finding: All type is one thin serif italic, small (about 3% of height), cream, placed next to the face/shoulder or across the figure's chest, appearing a few words at a time; key words are set in a much larger italic ('story.' fills the width at ~25% of height, 'backlash' stands alone). A different narrative register from the bold-condensed pieces of the same account.
why_it_works: size jump = emphasis; light italic suits serious subject

finding: Hard cut from the photoreal cinema lobby to a blank crumpled grey paper card with two lines of italic text ('here's what you need to know'), held ~1.3 s, then the next scene; the blank card is a breath between the intro and the story. Foreground blurred hats walk across to cover the cut in shot 1.
why_it_works: blank paper = pause
use_when: after a hook, before the body

finding: Roman soldier shot: slow push-in over a desk of scrolls, then a hand-drawn yellow-green loop traces around the head ('Odysseus' label) and finally the scroll prop is recoloured yellow-lime under the figure ('mastermind'). One scribble and one recolour carry the emphasis; no text box.
why_it_works: colour change on one prop

finding: Outro: top-down wooden desk with glasses, headphones, pencils and paper clips and a tablet showing the site; text 'If you want the project' appears left of the tablet; the tablet screen auto-scrolls. Camera slides sideways so the tablet crosses from right to centre.
why_it_works: same prop-desk CTA as other pieces (also Da2XkSfOy7h, DafS1lPu18x)

finding: Grade per scene: B&W-dim for the troubled moment (hand on face, dark stage, spotlights) and saturated mid-century palette (teal, orange, mustard) for the cheerful lobby with people on phones. Skin and fabric get a halftone dot overlay on every scene, soft vignette at the edges.
why_it_works: consistent halftone + vignette ties generated plates together

finding: Photoreal generated plates can drift in style (the Roman and the director look rendered differently); the piece hides it with the same grade, the same grain and no more than 1.5 s per plate.
why_it_works: short holds + same grade hide inconsistency

finding: Promo for a preset/sound pack: 12 shots (ASL 0.84 s) that each demo one effect: a flat-lay with bottles gets a tiny 'fx' tag cursor which triggers a change (bottle swaps colour); an airplane turns into the number '13 TEAMS'; football boots and years scroll; the suited walker swaps pose. The tag icon sits in the same place so the viewer knows the effect.
why_it_works: one recurring marker = this is the effect

finding: Number build: red '13' scales in with overshoot on a blue sky plate, plane moves behind it, 'TEAMS' in white follows below at 1/3 the size, a flock of birds flies up. The number, white label and birds are three separate pops with ~0.15 s stagger.
why_it_works: stagger reads as a spoken count

finding: Years list: a column of big pale year numerals on a grass ground scrolls vertically (1925, 1926 ... 1930) with the current year white and bold and the rest in 15% tint, a ball rolling beside it. Scroll with tint hierarchy = timeline without a line.
why_it_works: the current item is the only high-contrast one

finding: Walking man cut-out on brick street is a 2-pose cycle with a fixed-height lamp-post parallax; the same figure shows in DafS1lPu18x. The loop reads as a puppet which is fine for ≤1.5 s.
why_it_works: cheap walk loop

finding: End card: dark grey, white small caps header and an orange a COMMENT keyword keyword; the SD-card prop sits centre; type moves around the prop. Orange is the only colour.
why_it_works: single accent for the call to action

finding: Mostly white/cream paper grounds with a lot of empty space; one hero per frame (full-length cut-out of a woman on a red carpet with ropes, radio tower icon with pink waves, chalkboard in a wooden frame, gold-framed portrait). Hero sits in the lower 2/3 and the headline in the top third. Roughly 60-70% of the frame is empty paper.
why_it_works: empty paper makes each small prop a stand-alone symbol

finding: Scale-up cut from the full-body red-carpet figure to a blurred extreme close-up of her torso (cut 2: wide sharp to wide blurred zoom in ~1 frame), a hand-drawn arrow label 'her beauty' pointing at the face then sits in the close-up. Punch-in doubles as blur transition.
why_it_works: one object inside a scene gets the attention without cutting away

finding: Crumple-and-bin exit: the radio tower page crumples into a ball and drops into a green bin on a dark conveyor (photoreal, B&W background with the bin the only colour), cut to the bin carrying the tiny crumpled note. The idea is discarded literally. A hand-sized object leaves by a physical gag.
why_it_works: story beat 'ignored' becomes a visible action

finding: Blue pill labels ('Wi-Fi', then 'Bluetooth', then 'GPS') pop in one by one over concentric signal rings on black, each landing with ~0.4 s stagger and a small overshoot; rings keep expanding behind. Labels stack as a list that grows.
why_it_works: a growing list matches the enumeration

finding: Tiny serif/italic words (about 2% of height) appear one at a time on blank cream cards ('Just', 'Making', 'Films', 'Became', 'the', 'Foundation', 'Technologies'): ~0.4 s per word on an empty card, a sentence read as a word-per-card sequence. A different vein from stacked headlines.
why_it_works: one word per frame sets tempo; empty card makes the word the picture
use_when: deliver a line with deliberate pacing

finding: Whole piece has a scan-line / CRT texture and slight chromatic fringe over paper (horizontal fine lines visible in every frame), with colourised archive footage tinted warm and photos B&W; red carpet, pink wave and green bin are the only saturated accents.
why_it_works: vintage overlay + sparse accents

finding: Portrait in an ornate gold frame hung on a flat paper wall with a drop shadow, caption below in small serif; the frame slowly zooms to fill. Photo inside is colour from film still while the rest is monochrome.
why_it_works: frame gives a hard edge to a soft photo

finding: End card jumps to a silhouetted editor with headphones then a dark AE icon scene with cursor: tonal break from the paper world; fine here since it is an ad, but the story part never used dark UI.
why_it_works: separate CTA world

finding: One sepia/umber world for the whole piece: dark wood desk, aged paper, brass props, a vignette that darkens corners of every frame (spotlight-like oval), warm yellow-green lamp light. All plates are graded to the same 2-hue range (brown + olive) so photoreal generated people, drawings and logos match.
why_it_works: one grade and one vignette unify unrelated plates

finding: Dates are physical objects: an old ledger book flips open and the year numerals (1851, 1861, 1886, 1911, '70') sit on the page as the page-turn sequence; a hand stamps '1851' onto wood. The year changes by swapping the page; the book stays in place.
why_it_works: a book flipping pages is the timeline metaphor

finding: Name tags as paper labels: 'Elias' and 'Howe' appear as two curled paper strips pinned over the man's chest, then 'then ignored it' wraps a curved paper band across the sewing machine. Labels follow the subject's shape (curved, rotated ~5 deg) instead of straight captions.
why_it_works: type attached to the object
use_when: naming a person in a plate

finding: Smoke/dust wipe: the crowd scene dissolves through a drifting brown smoke layer into the 'World War I' text on cracked wood (cut 8: smoke layer is frame-wide, two parallel frames shown). Mask by smoke instead of a hard cut, the smoke edge moves ~1/3 of the frame per frame.
why_it_works: organic texture wipe in a sepia world

finding: The soldier is shot from above, cut-out on a pale tool-diagram ground (scissors, irons) so the figure is a 3D toy in a technical drawing; type 'THE MILITARY' peeks from behind. Then the scene tightens to the green jacket on a hanger lit by two lamps, the same colour family but darker.
why_it_works: a top-down view reads like a catalogue page

finding: Letters typed on a newspaper masthead ('Suddenly people noticed') with a hand-drawn light-bulb fist; mixed type per word: serif red 'Suddenly' large, small type 'people noticed' below, then the paper tilts and rolls to the next sentence. Word-by-word with a hand illustration alongside.
why_it_works: hand-drawn sketch + type = vintage poster

finding: Branding collage: a company badge, 1923 in a red hand-drawn circle, and two big boots cut out standing on a wooden floor; photos of the product pinned on corkboard with red thread and push-pins (3 clippings, tilted ±4 deg). Pins and thread connect items so clipping arrangement reads as evidence.
why_it_works: thread connects the evidence

finding: Outro opens the book: a closed ledger opens to reveal a phone mock-up in the right page and the call to action typed on the left; same prop as the date book at the beginning, so the piece closes on its opening device.
why_it_works: bookend

finding: Slower for this account: ASL 2.1 s, 4.5 events/10s. Holds are long where there is a detailed plate (people on a street, a desk), short for text-only beats; every plate has a slow zoom.
why_it_works: detailed plates need longer to read

finding: Hero is a B&W grain-graded plate with only the key prop in colour: the vacuum is yellow-lime on a grey living room, the sticky note yellow on a grey factory street. Colour on one object in monochrome plates = where the eye goes; the person stands lower centre with the empty background above him.
why_it_works: selective colour is the emphasis

finding: Light plane crosses a blue sky with the words 'he failed' pinned to its tail, then cut to the man in B&W with '5,126 times' small at his chest; the number line is small serif, not a counter graphic. Number is typed rather than counted.
why_it_works: restraint: number in small type is still the hook because the cut and the figure carry it
