finding: Top-down desk scene with real hand movements: a hand writes on paper in black pen ('he created 5,127'), the paper slides and the camera tracks; patent drawing sheets lie around at different tilts (stack with shadows). Hand footage composited so the writing is the animation.
why_it_works: human hand = scale and time

finding: Hard cut to a blank cream paper card with a lit oval (vignette) and single small words ('most people / would've / long / long before that') each on its own frame: a pause card as a beat after a long run of plates.
why_it_works: pacing: quiet sets up the payoff

finding: Yellow-black bold newspaper headline pasted on a folded newspaper page that rises into frame tilted ~12 deg over a darkened plate of the man ('JAMES DYSON CHANGES THE WAY WE CLEAN FOREVER'); subtitles stay small serif at the bottom. Prop-as-headline with the plate dimmed so the paper pops.
why_it_works: dimming the plate lets the prop be the only bright element

finding: Real interview footage (colour, shot in a studio) sits at the end after all the generated plates; subtitle styling stays the same (small serif italic with a shadow), so footage and plates share the caption layer. Frame is cropped tight to face.
why_it_works: caption layer is constant across source changes

finding: Halftone line grain and strong vignette on every B&W plate; yellow is the only accent (vacuum, note, highlighter, newspaper headline). Same yellow accent as DafS1lPu18x and DbAnBlpTkUQ.
why_it_works: account-wide palette

finding: Outro white grid desk with laptop, keyboard and phone; black chalk label with site; same prop-desk as DbagmfuIKyH. A clean white ground after dark plates reads as a reset.
why_it_works: light ground after dark

finding: Cut-out parts enter physically: a forearm swings an axe in from the top corner chopping red label logs on a tree stump (motion blur on the swing, label splits), then the whole Viking drops in with an axe and the word 'VIKINGS.' lands on the stump. Props are pieces of the title, so the title is the set.
why_it_works: a character action builds the title
use_when: title card that names the subject

finding: Dust/smoke cloud wipe (cut 8: a drifting brown cloud covers the whole frame in ~1 frame and hides the previous scene's text 'SCANDINAVIA'; next frame is pure smoke, next scene is born out of it). Also in DcJM47zIj-t (smoke wipe).
why_it_works: organic cover that suits aged paper
use_when: chapter change in a sepia piece

finding: Ground is a flat teal strip (sea) between cream sky and cream foreground: a three-band layout (cream top with title, teal middle with a row of longships, cream bottom). The ships are tiny and repeat; the closing shot enlarges one ship to 80% width. Scale jump from many small to one big.
why_it_works: many-to-one is the 'they arrive' beat

finding: Role words ('BRUTAL WARRIORS', 'EXPLORERS', 'TRADERS', 'SAILORS') are set in a dark red or black condensed serif title; each swaps while the same standing Viking figure on a stump stays at the same position and only his pose/props change (axe, map, anvil, shield). The word is on a signboard plate (brown wood, cream rim) for SAILORS. Persistent figure + swapping label = a list in one frame.
why_it_works: constant layout = viewer only reads the changing word

finding: The figure dissolves in from the paper with a particle/dust-disperse edge (cut 14: the body outline is made of grit that coalesces into the figure, top edge ragged, the stump bottom already solid). Entrance by dissolve, not pop.
why_it_works: materialising from paper fits the sepia world

finding: Antique map with a dotted route draws across the Atlantic and a timeline text '~1000AD / ~500 years / Columbus 1492' builds with a bracket and tick marks as numbers count up (968, 989, 999, 1000). Counting numerals and the dotted route are the only motion; the camera stays still.
why_it_works: a still map with one drawn line
use_when: a distance in time or space

finding: Last story beat switches from sepia to a B&W engraving look with a yellow tag label ('INTO IT') and a vignette that closes in (frame 4 of cut 24: blur plus iris-in). Desaturation signals the end of the story, and the one saturated item is the tag.
why_it_works: palette change = last line

finding: Text hitting the frame edge ('CENTUR', 'ATTACKED / VILLAGES' cut off at the edge) appears as an intermediate frame of an entrance; the cut-off is only in the first 2-3 frames. Final holds are always fully inside the safe margin.
why_it_works: edge crop only during motion

finding: Fisheye peephole: B&W stylised 3D delivery man with a round, bulging lens vignette (black corners, edge distortion) as if seen through a door spy hole; he holds a parcel to camera. The distorted circle is the whole picture and the corners are black. Then a hard cut to bright colour sky.
why_it_works: lens frame supplies a camera point of view without moving the camera

finding: Red 3D-looking bold type blasts onto a blue sky as a scale-in with stagger and the character rises on a floating island of rock, rocks falling off under it; Name and date appear in two separate plates ('IN 1888'...). Hovering island makes a pedestal and gives bob motion while he talks.
why_it_works: floating pedestal gives a stage and a motion loop

finding: Heavy red slab condensed type ('THE PEOPLE / HAD LIMITED ACCESS TO PRODUCTS') on a plain red ground with the head cut-out half in frame at the right; lines build and the line breaks are repositioned as new words come, with a quick horizontal jitter at each line change (glitch bars). Black plates use white/green/blue words ('A SIMPLE SOLUTION' in green, 'A NEW WAY' blue-outlined) so each beat has its own accent colour.
why_it_works: colour of the type is coded to the idea
use_when: text-only beats in a bold piece

finding: Dark-grey cards with a single word as spacer ('SO', 'IT', 'AND THE SECRET') in white or glowing text; each appears for ~0.3-0.5 s between image scenes with a soft glow and then the next scene starts from that word. Spacer cards break up the picture runs without a visual transition.
why_it_works: the word is the cut

finding: Product icons (watch with price tag '2$', underwear, hammer) each sit on a star-burst of spikes in a different colour (orange, purple, green) and swap every ~0.4 s with a coloured glow; house with a '1599$' price tag does the same at larger scale. Same swap template, different colour per product.
why_it_works: template + colour rotation = list of items

finding: Parallax street scene: a miniature house with a road and mailbox in a diorama look; a truck drives across the lower strip with motion blur while the camera pushes in ~1.1; text 'AND WAIT FOR IT TO ARRIVE' slides on the road in perspective. Type placed in the scene's ground plane.
why_it_works: perspective text sits in the world

finding: Mixed styles (stylised 3D puppet, fisheye B&W, neon icons, flat text cards) inside 40 s. It holds because each style has one colour world (red, blue sky, black) and the transitions are word cards; without the cards it would look like a mashup.
why_it_works: separators between style changes
use_when: avoid more than 2 styles per piece

finding: CRT scanline and film-grain over all dark cards; red felt-like ground in the red scenes (visible woven texture); sky photo for blue scenes. Soft vignette on every frame.
why_it_works: texture on flat colour

finding: Gallery-wall world: a dim wood-panelled corridor with a single picture lamp; the subject painting hangs as the only bright thing (lamp cone lights the canvas from above, rest of frame ~80% brown shadow). Date '1892' is stamped on the wall in the same light. The lit canvas is the focal point by value contrast, not by size.
why_it_works: a picture lamp is a built-in spotlight

finding: Cloud wipe opens the piece: white cloud bank moves down and off the frame (cut 1) to reveal the man at the easel, with a thin serif title 'What if Fear' dropping in at red/white. The cloud edge is the transition and the reveal.
why_it_works: same cloud as a wipe device (see DZuVqDpO0Um sky)

finding: The painting swings in on a cord (rotates ~15 deg and settles in 4 frames), then slow push-in to fill the frame; the next scene has it wall-hung at the same spot but with a heavier push (zoom ~2x) and a blurred foreground.
why_it_works: pendulum settle gives the frame life with one object

finding: Four copies of the painting hang on a white wall in a 2x2 grid with small rotations (±3 deg) and different colour grades (blue, green, red) each; the grid slides sideways and one picture scales out. Variation through colour grade, not through layout; identical size and spacing.
why_it_works: identical layout makes small colour differences the content

finding: A grey tape/redaction strip with a red glow wipes across the painting's sky ('four versions...') and a hand with a pencil draws on a green cutting mat under the painting. Tape = censorship / hidden note; the hand and pencil drive the reveal. Match with DcaqrJkOiD3 hand writing.
why_it_works: physical hand agent
use_when: a hidden note or edit in an image

finding: Scattered words (it / a / symbol / became / of / fear / itself) drift around a bright centre point on dark grain and then fly together into the word 'EDITORS' (letters spin in from different angles and lock). Reading order is by scatter, then assemble. Used for the final statement and the CTA brand.
why_it_works: scatter-to-lockup conveys 'became' visually
use_when: a closing statement that becomes the brand

finding: Colour comes from the painting alone: the orange/blue of the canvas against brown wood, white wall, green mat or teal spotlight backdrop. Each scene's ground is chosen to complement the painting (brown to white to green to teal).
why_it_works: ground rotates, hero stays; saturation of the hero stays highest
use_when: one hero object across many beats

finding: Word labels around the painting ('Oil', 'Pastel', 'Paper') float at the edge of the frame at ~2% type size and partly overlap the frame; legibility is poor because they are tiny and the picture is bright. Better pieces pair a label with a leader line or box.
why_it_works: leader lines tie label to object

finding: Calm tempo: ASL 1.5 s, 6.4 events/10s, with 28 shots of which many are sub-second swaps inside the grid sequence and ~2 s holds on the lit painting.
why_it_works: holds on the hero, bursts for variants

finding: One stage metaphor per beat, each a full-frame paper tableau: sun-and-clouds sky, harlequin-diamond curtain frame, ticket booth on a black/white sunburst floor, Van Gogh swirl wallpaper with gilt frames. Every scene = flat painted/engraved backdrop + 1 hero cut-out + 1-2 small props; the hero sits on the central vertical axis with the lower third left for the floor/pattern.
why_it_works: A dense, patterned backdrop is tolerated because the hero is a different material (photographic/engraved, desaturated) and the type is white with a dark edge; pattern frequency is high, value contrast is low
use_when: each line needs a place (booth, wall, stage) rather than an object floating on colour

finding: Scene-to-scene is a prop-driven wipe, not a dissolve: the joker card slides up and the sunburst page folds/slides away to reveal the harlequin frame; later the curtain frame becomes the new set. Each exit object is the entrance of the next scene.
why_it_works: Match-cut on a physical object keeps one world and gives the motion a reason
use_when: between two metaphors in the same 'theatre' world

finding: Slow constant push-in on the booth (zoom 1.09, pan -9/-15px/360, easing peak at start) while the Batman cut-out stands still; parallax comes from foreground curtains (move faster, larger) vs. booth vs. floor. Then tarot cards stack in over it, each pushed ~0.27s apart.
why_it_works: Three depth layers at different speeds sell a 3D stage from flat paper; tiny zoom avoids reading as a digital scale
use_when: a held hero while props arrive

finding: Tarot cards (MONEY, POWER, RESPECT) enter one per ~0.4s with a small slide-up plus drop shadow, then the camera pulls out (zoom 0.78-0.9) so the cards become frames on a wall of frames — the previous scene is literally hung inside the next.
why_it_works: The pull-out reveals the previous scene as an object in the next: continuous space, cheap 'cut'
use_when: list of 3 qualities then a summary line

finding: Fast stretch: 14 events in ~5s, shot length 0.27s (8 frames at 30fps) = beat grid, mostly holds/drifts of the same wall while frames swap and the pull-out continues; then a long calm 3.4s rotate (-3.7 deg) shot on the oval frame with chain swing.
why_it_works: Fast cuts are small changes inside one set, so it reads as motion not chaos; the long hold lands the key portrait
use_when: when a list resolves into one idea

finding: Type is white condensed grotesque, bold, tracked, set centred on top of the artwork with a red ellipse scribble around the key phrase (BY HIS PAST); words appear in chunks of 2-3 and sit on the object plane (a plank/sign in booth scenes) rather than floating.
why_it_works: Heavy sans over ornate art gives the one clear contrast level; the scribble adds hand-made emphasis consistent with paper

finding: Per-scene palette is locked: sun scene mint+orange; theatre red/black/white; wall blue+gilt; Joker act brown wood/green/red; finale white graph paper with grey objects. Joker act swaps to a wooden table with newspaper clippings, hand holding a card, plastic mask — real photographed props with soft shadows.
why_it_works: Colour changes with the metaphor, so a palette switch reads as a chapter break

finding: The Joker footage and film stills switch from paper world to a dark photo grade with halftone lines; the pieces avoid the 'cheap' look by keeping a visible line/halftone texture on photo stills so they match the engravings.
why_it_works: Texture on photos unifies stills with engraved art
use_when: mixing film stills into paper scenes

finding: Outro: graph-paper desk with calculator, keyboard, cards in the corners; 'EDITORS' letters type on in the empty centre; three AE badges pop in staggered, then yellow brand slate with wordmark growing. Negative space is kept for the type, props pushed to corners and cropped by the frame edge.
why_it_works: Cropping props at the edge frames the centre; flat yellow slate resets and brands

finding: Match-on-object cuts through a story: aerial aisle -> chips bag held to a black circular vignette (radial halftone) -> back of bag -> POV scanner at till; the product is the through-line and each shot re-grabs it in a new framing.
why_it_works: A single hero object across shots keeps continuity while locations change

finding: The black disc with ring of tick marks (a barcode turned radial) is the isolating device: the busy aisle photo is cut away to a dark plate so the bag reads, then the plate becomes the full background.
why_it_works: Dark plate behind a bright red/yellow pack = max value contrast, nothing else competes
use_when: isolating a hero in a busy photo

finding: Photo shots (shopkeeper, hands, till) use slow push-in 1.05-1.15 plus soft focus roll (blur to sharp in two frames) and heavy film grain; ending the shot by blurring/darkening into the next plate.
why_it_works: Rack-focus on stills fakes camera depth

finding: Archive newspaper (1974 headline): wood-table texture is shown first with a year number on it, newspaper drops in at an angle with shadow, camera pushes with a vignette lens circle that darkens edges like a magnifier, then a scanner device enters from the corner.
why_it_works: The archive piece has paper edge, curl and tilt so it reads as a real object; a circular vignette = 'looking at evidence'

finding: Word-by-word kinetic: 'it' 'almost' 'insignificant' placed one per beat in the same spot of a dark plate, next to the red laser scanner cone; later big slab type (FASTER) with extrusion on a white pill/sticker shape on red.
why_it_works: One word per beat on a fixed spot makes timing the message

finding: Hand holding scanner in front of a big jar on a white torn-paper edge over a red band; UI-card overlay (INVENTORY 36) pinned to the jar: the paper tear is the transition (white fills from the top as hard rectangles stepping down in 3 blocks).
why_it_works: Block-wipe in the colour of the next scene

finding: Whole piece is graded dark/warm with grain and halftone dots; light scenes (barcode on off-white, white paper) are used once for the title card and the CTA, creating a dark->light shift for the payoff.
why_it_works: A single light scene feels like an exhale at the reveal

finding: Monochrome halftone cut-outs (face, skull, mannequin head, lipstick, microscope, coins) all in grey on a single deep red ground; the only colour is the red ground and a few red accents (dotted marks on the face, red cross-hatch scribbles). Faces are photos, props are engravings.
why_it_works: One hue + grey means any element can be dropped anywhere without clashing; style unity comes from palette, not from the objects
use_when: fast collage with many unrelated objects

finding: Big serif display caps (distressed) in off-white with a soft glow, one phrase per beat, often cut by the frame (AGING cropped to GING), scale changes with each beat; small spaced secondary words (DECADES 1941, WRINKLES) act as texture.
why_it_works: Serif + glow stays legible on red; tiny labels add the editorial 'annotated' look

finding: Photo faces swap in place in 1-2 frames (old woman -> man skull -> older face) while the type stays; wipe via circular lens/ring lines; the matched position keeps the eye still while the content changes.
why_it_works: Hold the anchor, swap the content
use_when: list of examples inside one idea

finding: Scribble underlines, dotted wrinkle marks and a speech-bubble circle with arrow draw on over 0.3-0.5s; toothpaste/serum shots animate liquid in halftone with large glossy droplets sliding on the layer above.
why_it_works: Hand-drawn marks make the cut-outs feel annotated

finding: Continuous push-in or pull-out nearly all the time (peak at start): mannequin face zooms 1.2x while text builds; microscope reveal pulls from the head (halftone) to a warm spotlight cone on the word — the only warm light in the piece.
why_it_works: Spotlight = the key word; one warm accent in a cold palette

finding: Pieces rise from below or scale up from 0.8 to 1.0 with glow; exits are a dissolve into the red; the heart/FEAR beat fades through into AE badge stack and brand text.
why_it_works: Ease-out scale with glow reads as 'appearing' on red

finding: Heavy, slow pull-outs with roll (rot to -20 deg, zoom 0.65-0.77) on the poster and the hospital scenes, then big push-in 1.56 across 4.4s; the camera is never still. Peak-at near start or end, meaning ease-in/out curves.
why_it_works: Roll + zoom on a still keeps AI images alive and hides the lack of parallax

finding: Red-white label stickers (name tags) pinned over faces: JORDAN BELFORT, JONAH HILL change by cuts; yellow torn-paper label 'Vitamin-B' on the cocaine line; label has paper edge and slight tilt. 'FAKE COCAINE' as 3D red block type on the building.
why_it_works: Name tags/stickers = documentary caption that belongs to the scene

finding: Dissolve/zoom transitions: scene 3 enters with a white light flash and a square window that grows (the new image appears inside a bright rectangle then fills the frame); the X-ray/organs overlay is introduced by a glow reveal.
why_it_works: A square reveal makes a mask-in cut; the white flash hides the swap
use_when: moving to a related medical/zoom-in idea

finding: Dark blue textile bg with 'But it gets CRAZIER' small serif in the middle: huge negative space between chapters; then a gallery wall with poster; then a map of Malaysia built from torn red paper on white with type typed top-left.
why_it_works: A plain text card acts as a breath, resets attention before the bigger claim

finding: Newspaper clipping slides in on a brown surface with a drop shadow, folds at the corner, stays slightly angled; then a TV scene with the man seen from behind (photo) -> TV image zooms until it fills the screen, match cut to the next red plate.
why_it_works: Zoom through a screen = natural match cut

finding: Hand-over to brand: off-white page with dark red/black block title; phone mockup slides up with cursor notch growing out of the dynamic-island that expands to a pill; app screens scroll inside.
why_it_works: Phone is the only 3D object, so it stands out as the CTA

finding: Clay/figure-style 3D photographed miniatures on a red-painted backdrop with a black sun disc and a gold disc behind: low-angle side-on shot, ground strip at the bottom third, figures fighting on it; the camera stays at ground level.
why_it_works: Real depth of field and a stage sells miniature; negative space above the fighters

finding: Cuts between rich 'stage' shots to tight face close-ups with the ground blurred; angle changes by 1 cut: wide of Caesar at desk -> push-in over-the-shoulder to Caesar + old man. Shot lengths 2-5s, longer than the other pieces; rhythm is dialogue-like.
why_it_works: Wide-to-close cut = classic scene coverage

finding: Torn white paper strip with a drip-like edge drops across the lower part of a fortune-teller shot, wiping to the next scene: a paper tear transition with visible fibre and shadow.
why_it_works: A material wipe in the same world

finding: Diagram cards: a portrait on parchment with connector lines branching to six small busts — lines draw over ~0.4s, nodes pop in stagger. Then a hand-held dagger enters from the right, 3D, and stabs a heart; numeral '22' in white serif glows over it.
why_it_works: Stagger + line draw = readable hierarchy

finding: Parchment page with a hand writing in the lower corner (real hand + pen photographed), text blurs in then sharpens; headline 'BLADES HIDDEN' in white stamp-like type breaking at the bottom edge.
why_it_works: Real hand in frame gives 'author' reading

finding: Fully photo-real AI street and market scenes (autumn leaves framing the top corners, blue sky, warm light) with hero a small tulip: the leaf/foliage in the top 15% is a repeated frame element across scenes.
why_it_works: A repeated foreground frame unifies different scenes

finding: Red cloth plate with grey halftone hands (key + tulip) = 'chapter' card in the red; then cut to the street; a white fog-out ends the market scene and a red plate begins the next beat. Plates alternate red / yellow / dark-grunge.
why_it_works: Flat colour plates re-set attention between photo scenes

finding: Yellow glowing tulip bar chart with growing bars; 'RARE BULBS' in heavy stencil, black type on yellow ground ('THEN CONFIDENCE COLLAPSED' in black on yellow, tight tracking, letters dropping). Black on yellow, white on red, nothing else.
why_it_works: Fixed type colours per ground

finding: Slow pushes in each photo scene with a slight tilt; a red balloon lifts a tulip over the town (lens zoom out), earth with tulips growing as a globe: scale jumps from market to planet within one cut (match on a round object).
why_it_works: Round-shape match cut changes scale in 1 frame

finding: End: AE icon with a particle dust scatter-in on yellow, then brand text beside it; heading letters assemble from dust. The dust directs the eye to the badge.
why_it_works: Particles as an entrance for a flat icon

finding: Night-sky paper world: navy ground with cut-paper clouds (engraved lines) and gold stars at the corners; a dark hero rises from the bottom third; logo/lettering at the top. The clouds' dark outline + gold star shape repeat in 4 scenes.
why_it_works: Repeat of 2 motifs ties scenes

finding: Curtain opens/closes as a wipe (red velvet from both sides) and cards on green felt: a hand holds a card fan, then cards deal; the Doom card flips (scale X 1 -> 0 -> 1) to reveal the next one.
why_it_works: Flip is a swap with a real-world reason

finding: Cards drop onto the felt one after another (~0.3s) with drop-shadow; the hand exits down; the small text in a script font writes on beside them, cropped by the edge.
why_it_works: Staggered props give rhythm without cuts

finding: Mix of two registers: tarot/theatre paper scenes (navy/red/green) then dark film-grade stills of Doom (green cape, ember sky). The photographic scenes carry the claim, the paper scenes carry the form.
why_it_works: Switching register for the key claim

finding: Pinned outro: sparse navy plate with cloud, 'EDITORS WHO' type centre-left with AE badges; then flat yellow brand slate. Same plate as the opening, closing the loop.
why_it_works: Bookend

finding: Subtitle line in the lower third in clean sans, word-by-word, over portrait/stage photo with heavy vignette and scanlines; huge '$8 Billion' bleeds over the left/right edges behind the person's head (type behind the subject).
why_it_works: Type behind the cut-out = depth

finding: Glitch/RGB-split and block-mosaic reveals: a white rectangle opens in a dark plate and fills the frame with the next image; a diagonal wipe line with chromatic edge (blue/magenta) between logo plates.
why_it_works: Short glitch hides AI-image swaps

finding: Orange cork-board desk with 3 photos pinned at angles and a pen, 'Same Company' type on top; then cards tumble. Dense small items on a flat colour.
why_it_works: Pinboard = evidence

finding: Founder photos swap in the same position with a giant condensed word (NVIDIA / LOVABLE) behind them, 1 per ~0.4s; the word changes, the body stays centred.
why_it_works: Position-locked swaps

finding: Isometric cartoon skyscraper on a cloud, stretching up as a '$50M REVENUE' sign appears; scene then pulls into a western 'COMPANIES FOR SALE' storefront; later slot machine 777 with red curtains and a money stack dropped by a hand. Each metaphor is a different render style joined by hard cuts at ~2s.
why_it_works: Metaphor changes with the claim

finding: Ends on empty cream plate (no content) with tiny serif lines — a text-only sentence lets the phone mockup rise below. The earlier busy shots make this empty frame feel intentional.

Contest promo: pixel/Minecraft-style 3D renders (trophies, desks, calculator keyboard) with a stable dark teal palette and gold type; paper pieces appear only in the brand beats (graph paper, yellow label). Lower relevance for collage.
Radial speed-blur burst (a few frames of blue/yellow streak) as a cut between calendar paper and the pixel hero; whip-style transition.
